articles.title: North Texas vs UTSA: The Mean Green Fight Back but Can't Catch A'Marion Peterson
articles.byline: Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, The North Texas Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UTSA Roadrunners (8-2) 35, North Texas Mean Green (7-3) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Alamodome, San Antonio. Next: at Tulane, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans
articles.text:
Mean Green fans, I believed right up until the end. UTSA 35, North Texas 16. That was Saturday night at the Alamodome. It leaves us at 7-3. We cut it to 21-16 with 8:32 left. We had a real chance. And then their running back broke two long touchdown runs, and it was gone.

The start was rough. Early in the first quarter, one of our throws was intercepted and returned for a touchdown. In the second quarter, Baron Tipton made a terrific 49-yard catch, but the ball came loose at the end of it, and UTSA recovered. By halftime it was 21-3.

But this team doesn't quit. Chris Jimerson Jr. gave us a spark. In the third quarter, he found Max Reese for a 16-yard touchdown. Then midway through the fourth, he ran it in himself from 9 yards. The two-point try failed, but it was 21-16, and our section was rocking. Jimerson finished 7 of 12 for 70 yards and ran for 33.

Dominic De Freitas made a 31-yard field goal in the second quarter. Max Reese caught three balls for 50 yards. Tipton had 63 yards on two grabs. Our defense made some plays too. Zakye Barker made 12 tackles, Aaron Alexander had a sack and a half, and Brandon Jones made two tackles for loss. Brenden Reese intercepted a throw in the third quarter. Ian Ratliff punted beautifully all night.

But we committed 13 penalties for 93 yards, and we came up short on fourth down twice in the final five minutes. You can't do that on the road against an 8-2 team.

Seven and three is still a great season. Let's go finish it, and let's do it with the same fight we showed in that fourth quarter.

Go Mean Green! The North Texas Mean Green travel to face Tulane in New Orleans, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: UTSA vs North Texas: A'Marion Peterson Runs for Four Touchdowns at the Alamodome
articles.matchup: Final: UTSA Roadrunners (8-2) 35, North Texas Mean Green (7-3) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Alamodome, San Antonio. Next: at UAB, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Protective Stadium, Birmingham
articles.text:
Birds Up, San Antonio! UTSA 35, North Texas 16 on Saturday night at the Alamodome, and we're 8-2 and unbeaten at home. A'Marion Peterson put on a show I'll be talking about for years.

Eleven carries. One hundred seventy-nine yards. Four touchdowns. Peterson scored from 47 yards in the second quarter, from 2 yards right before halftime, and then he iced it in the fourth with runs of 38 and 46 yards. Every time North Texas got close, he broke another one. I lost count of how many times I high-fived the guy behind me.

And the defense got us started. In the first quarter, Bryce Grays hurried a throw, and RJ Lester Jr. picked it off and ran it back 9 yards for a touchdown. Later in the second quarter, Owen Pewee punched the ball loose after a 49-yard catch, and Ahamad Chapman fell on it. That swing kept North Texas off the board.

It got tight in the second half. North Texas scored twice and cut it to 21-16 with 8:32 left. But then Peterson went 38 yards with 3:24 to go, and the Alamodome exploded. Our defense then got two fourth-down stops in a row. E. Baldwin and Grays combined on a sack on the first one, and Joel Rogers made the tackle short of the marker on the second.

Will Henderson III ran for 70 yards, and we finished with 241 on the ground. Owen McCown didn't have a big night through the air, but he didn't have to. Darion White made eight tackles. Pewee had seven, and Grays had seven with a tackle and a half for loss.

Eight and two. This team is rolling, and San Antonio is loving it.

Birds Up! The UTSA Roadrunners travel to face UAB in Birmingham, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: South Carolina vs Arkansas: Four Turnovers End the Winning Streak in Fayetteville
articles.byline: Beaumont 'Beau' Cheraw, The South Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Arkansas Razorbacks (4-6) 34, South Carolina Gamecocks (6-4) 6, Sat., Nov. 14, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville. Next: vs Georgia, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Gamecock fans, that one was ugly, and I'm going to own it. Arkansas 34, South Carolina 6. That was Saturday night in Fayetteville. It leaves us at 6-4. Our four-game winning streak is gone. We turned it loose four times, and Arkansas made us pay for nearly every one.

We played without LaNorris Sellers, and Cutter Woods went the whole way at quarterback. He threw for 271 yards on 24 of 43, and he never stopped trying. But three of his throws were intercepted, and one of them, in the third quarter, went back 63 yards for an Arkansas touchdown. We also lost a fumble in the second quarter. That's the game right there.

There were moments. Jabree Coleman ran 16 times for 77 yards and scored on a 3-yard run in the third quarter. He caught six balls too. Mazeo Bennett Jr. had a 51-yard catch that got the visiting section up. Donovan Murph and Maurice Brown II each had big grabs. We moved the ball for 369 yards. We just couldn't finish drives.

Fred Johnson was everywhere on defense with 13 tackles. Peyton Williams made 10, and David Bucey made eight. Justin Okoronkwo had a sack, and Gerald Kilgore broke up a throw. They were on the field a long time and kept fighting.

We also missed a field goal in the first quarter, failed a two-point try and came up short on fourth down twice late. Twelve penalties for 91 yards didn't help us one bit either.

Six and four. It is still a good season, and we're already bowl eligible. This team won four straight before tonight, and it can bounce back. Let's go get the big one at home.

Let's make Columbia rock. Go Gamecocks! The South Carolina Gamecocks host Georgia at Williams-Brice Stadium, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Arkansas vs South Carolina: Joker Johnson Takes Two Away, and the Hogs Finally Win a Big One at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Arkansas Razorbacks (4-6) 34, South Carolina Gamecocks (6-4) 6, Sat., Nov. 14, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville. Next: at Texas, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin
articles.text:
Woo Pig Sooie! Arkansas 34, South Carolina 6 on Saturday night at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, and we're 4-6. That's our first SEC win at home since Nov. 5, 2024, against Tennessee, and it's the first time we've beaten a ranked team since that same night. I called the Hogs until my voice gave out.

Joker Johnson was the hero of the night. He intercepted two throws, and in the third quarter he jumped a route at our 37 and went 63 yards the other way for a touchdown. 24-6. The whole stadium lost its mind. Ben Bogle added another interception in the fourth and broke up a fourth-down throw later. We forced four turnovers and didn't give the ball away once.

KJ Jackson was sharp. Fifteen of 24 for 188 yards and two touchdowns, both in the second quarter. He found Chris Marshall for 23 yards and then Antonio Jordan for 28 on the very next drive. 17-0 at halftime. Max Gilbert added field goals from 31 and 30 yards. Sutton Smith ran in a 7-yard score late, and Cam Settles ran for 64 yards.

The defense held South Carolina to one touchdown. Ja'Quavion Smith had a sack. Khmori House and Charlie Collins each hurried the quarterback twice. Bradley Shaw made seven tackles. They stopped two fourth-down tries in the fourth quarter.

This season has been rough, and I'm not going to pretend one night fixes all of it. But beating a ranked team at home by 28? That's a night I'll remember. I hugged a man I've never met, and he hugged me right back, and neither of us could stop grinning.

Let's go make some noise in Austin. Woo Pig! The Arkansas Razorbacks travel to face Texas in Austin, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Purdue vs Iowa: A Late First-Half Touchdown Can't Spark the Boilers at Kinnick
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa Hawkeyes (8-2) 28, Purdue Boilermakers (3-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City. Next: vs Wisconsin, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette
articles.text:
Boiler fans, I'm going to keep this one honest. Iowa 28, Purdue 7. That was Saturday night at Kinnick Stadium. It leaves us at 3-7. Seven points is our lowest of the season, and it was a long night in Iowa City.

We had a moment. Down 14-0 late in the second quarter, Ryan Browne found George Burhenn for a 3-yard touchdown with 1:49 left before halftime. 14-7, and our little corner of Kinnick got loud. Then, with five seconds left in the half, Iowa threw a short one that turned into a 44-yard touchdown. That one stung. 21-7 at the break.

Browne went 14 of 23 for 158 yards. Asaad Waseem was our best weapon, with six catches for 93 yards, including a 34-yarder. Fame Ijeboi ran for 64 yards and caught three balls. Xavier Townsend had three grabs for 39.

The defense actually made some plays. Iowa missed three field goals, and K. Burgos blocked one of them. Charles Correa made 10 tackles and two tackles for loss. John Slaughter had eight tackles, seven of them solo, and Justin Denson had eight too. Jojo Hayden made seven stops. They were on the field for more than 35 minutes, and Iowa ran for 246 yards.

We came up short on fourth down twice in the fourth quarter, including at the Iowa 10 late, and we threw an interception in their end zone in the third. We also missed a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter. When you're playing on the road against an 8-2 team, you can't leave those points out there.

Three and seven is tough. But I'll be back next week, and I'll be loud. These players keep showing up, and so will I.

Boiler Up! The Purdue Boilermakers host Wisconsin at Ross-Ade Stadium, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Iowa vs Purdue: Hank Brown and LJ Phillips Keep November Golden at Kinnick
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa Hawkeyes (8-2) 28, Purdue Boilermakers (3-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City. Next: at Illinois, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign
articles.text:
Hawkeye fans, November in Iowa City is a beautiful thing. Iowa 28, Purdue 7 on Saturday night at Kinnick Stadium, and we're 8-2. That makes three wins in a row. We waved to the kids at the children's hospital, and then we went out and took care of business.

Hank Brown ran for a touchdown and threw for another. He snuck in from 1 yard late in the first quarter to open the scoring, and with five seconds left before halftime, he threw a short one to Braeden Jackson, who turned it into a 44-yard touchdown. 21-7 at the break. Brown said it was just an all-around team win. He's right.

LJ Phillips Jr. ran 23 times for 123 yards, his second straight 100-yard game. Tony Diaz scored on a 14-yard run in the second quarter and caught five balls. Then, early in the third, Xavier Williams broke a 48-yard touchdown run, and that was that. We ran for 246 yards and finished with 434. Ten of 15 on third down. That's Iowa football, and I wouldn't trade it for anything.

The defense held Purdue to its lowest scoring night of the season. Zach Lutmer made 10 tackles and intercepted a throw in our end zone in the third quarter. Cam Buffington made eight stops. Jayden Montgomery had seven. And late in the fourth, Lutmer and Kahmari Brown stuffed a fourth-down run at our 10.

Now, I have to be honest. Caden Buhr missed three field goals, one of them blocked. I still love him. Everybody has a night.

Coach Kirk Ferentz said November is an important month, and it comes down to good preparation. We've now won 25 of our last 30 games in November. That's no accident. That's a program that knows exactly who it is.

Go Hawks! The Iowa Hawkeyes travel to face Illinois in Champaign, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET.

articles.title: New Mexico vs UNLV: A 14-0 Lead Gets Away in Front of a Ranked Home Crowd
articles.byline: Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, The New Mexico Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UNLV Rebels (6-4) 21, New Mexico Lobos (8-2) 17, Sat., Nov. 14, University Stadium (NM), Albuquerque. Next: at Wyoming, Fri., Nov. 20, 9:00 PM ET, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie
articles.text:
Lobo fans, this one is going to sit with me for a while. UNLV 21, New Mexico 17. That was Saturday night at University Stadium. It leaves us at 8-2. It was our first home game as a ranked team, 37,440 of us showed up, and we let a 14-0 lead get away. That's a tough night in Albuquerque.

The start was everything I wanted. Scottre Humphrey ran it in from 3 yards in the first quarter, and Toa Fa'avae found Cade Keith for a 9-yard touchdown in the second. 14-0, and University Stadium was rocking. Humphrey finished with 89 yards on 19 carries, and Kiefer Sibley added 77. We ran for 203 yards. Bailen George, who also caught two balls, completed a 65-yard throw too.

Then the offense stalled. Nick Romero made a 36-yard field goal in the third quarter to make it 17-7, and that was our last score. UNLV hit a 43-yard touchdown early in the fourth, then their quarterback ran 44 yards for the lead with 7:26 left. We had two chances after that. We came up short on fourth down at the UNLV 23, and with 1:31 left, Fa'avae threw an interception at our 23. The play was reviewed, and the call stood.

The defense still had its moments. Darren Agu sacked their quarterback and forced a fumble in the first quarter. Frankie Edwards III intercepted a throw in the third. Austin Brawley made six tackles and hurried the quarterback twice. Mercury Swaim had six stops too.

Eight and two is still a season to be proud of, and this team has given us so many great nights already. This one just hurts because it was right there, and we all felt it slipping.

Short week. Let's bounce back, Lobos. The New Mexico Lobos travel to face Wyoming in Laramie, Friday, Nov. 20, 9 PM ET.

articles.title: UNLV vs New Mexico: Jackson Arnold Rallies the Rebels Past the No. 23 Lobos
articles.matchup: Final: UNLV Rebels (6-4) 21, New Mexico Lobos (8-2) 17, Sat., Nov. 14, University Stadium (NM), Albuquerque. Next: at San José State, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:00 PM ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose
articles.text:
Rebel fans, I have rarely been prouder of this team. UNLV 21, New Mexico 17 on Saturday night at University Stadium in Albuquerque, and we're 6-4. We beat the No. 23 team in the country on the road, we came back from 14-0, and we spoiled their first home game as a ranked team. That's a Rebels night.

Jackson Arnold was the reason. He threw for 201 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 98 more, including the winner. Late in the first half, he found Keyan Burnett for a 16-yard score to make it 14-7. Then in the fourth quarter, he hit Kayden McGee for 43 yards to cut it to 17-14, and with 7:26 left, he took a quarterback draw 44 yards to the house. 21-17. I jumped so high I almost lost my hat.

McGee finished with two catches for 64 yards. Vincent Carner had a 37-yard grab. The defense was just as big. Cam Santee made 12 tackles, a sack and 2.5 tackles for loss. Andre Porter added a sack. And late, with New Mexico driving, Tony-Louis Nkuba intercepted a throw at their 23 with 1:31 left, and the call stood after a review. That was the dagger.

We also stopped them on fourth down late in the fourth quarter, with 3:53 left, to get the ball back. Denver Harris, Kamuela Ka'aihue and Dee Crayton each made seven tackles. We did lose a fumble and throw an interception, so it wasn't perfect. It didn't have to be.

Six and four, with a ranked road win. That's five straight wins for us in New Mexico's building, too. That's who we are.

Keep it rolling, Rebels! One more road trip, one more chance. The UNLV Rebels travel to face San José State in San Jose, Nov. 21, 7 PM ET.

articles.title: Virginia Tech vs Stanford: A 21-0 Hole Is Too Much to Climb at Lane Stadium
articles.byline: Ruthanne Dellinger, The Virginia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Stanford Cardinal (5-5) 40, Virginia Tech Hokies (6-4) 22, Sat., Nov. 14, Lane Stadium, Blacksburg. Next: at Miami, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Hokie fans, that was not the night I expected at Lane Stadium. Stanford 40, Virginia Tech 22 on Saturday, and we're 6-4. We gave the ball away three times in the first half, fell behind 21-0, and spent the rest of the night chasing. That's on us.

Charlie Eckhardt was a one-man wrecking crew against us. He intercepted two throws in the first quarter and forced a fumble in the second that Stanford recovered at our 29. They scored 14 points off those takeaways. You can't do that at home and expect a different result.

There were still some bright spots, and I want to talk about them. Jeffrey Overton Jr. ran 19 times for 107 yards and scored from 2 yards late in the second quarter. Ethan Grunkemeyer threw for 270 yards and two touchdowns, including a 69-yard strike to Davion Brown in the third quarter that made it 24-14 and got Lane loud again. Que'Sean Brown caught six balls for 71 yards and a 9-yard touchdown in the fourth, and we added a two-point conversion. Marlion Jackson had a 49-yard catch.

Keon Wylie made 11 tackles. Isaiah Brown-Murray and Tyson Flowers each had seven stops. We converted 3 of 5 on fourth down and finished with 398 yards. The offense wasn't the whole problem on this night.

And Stanford's kicker made all four of his field goal tries, including a 49-yarder. Every time we got close, those points pushed the lead back out. We never attempted a field goal ourselves, which tells you how the night went.

Six and four is still a good season, and we're already bowl eligible. Let's finish it the right way, together, all the way to the end.

Let's go, Hokies! The Virginia Tech Hokies travel to face Miami in Miami Gardens, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Stanford vs Virginia Tech: Micah Ford and Charlie Eckhardt End a Long Road Drought
articles.matchup: Final: Stanford Cardinal (5-5) 40, Virginia Tech Hokies (6-4) 22, Sat., Nov. 14, Lane Stadium, Blacksburg. Next: at California, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley
articles.text:
Cardinal fans, I have been waiting a long time to write this one. Stanford 40, Virginia Tech 22 on Saturday night at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg, and we're 5-5. That's our first road win since Sept. 20, 2024, at Syracuse, and it ends a 15-game road losing streak, the longest in school history. I yelled so loud I scared the person next to me, and then I hugged them, and then we both yelled together.

Micah Ford was a wrecking ball. Twenty-seven carries, 149 yards and three touchdowns, from 3, 5 and 2 yards. Davis Warren added a 16-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. We ran for 233 yards and didn't give it away once. That's how you win on the road.

And then there's Charlie Eckhardt. He caused all three Virginia Tech turnovers in the first half. He intercepted two throws, forced a fumble that Jay Green recovered at the Hokies 29, and also made 10 tackles and a sack. Fourteen points came off those takeaways, and we led 24-7 at halftime. Sam Mattingly made nine tackles, and Jay Green added eight and two breakups.

Emmet Kenney was perfect. Four field goals, from 31, 46, 49 and 23 yards. Sixteen points all by himself. Caden High and Nico Brown each caught five balls, and Benji Blackburn had a 30-yard grab. We finished with 436 yards and scored 40 points, our most in an ACC game since we joined the league.

Virginia Tech hit a 69-yard touchdown in the third quarter and a late score in the fourth. We answered every time. This team is tough, and I'm so proud. Five and five, and for the first time in a long time, the road doesn't scare us.

The Big Game. Go Cardinal! The Stanford Cardinal travel to face California in Berkeley, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Florida Atlantic vs Tulsa: Caden Veltkamp Throws for 340, but the Big Plays Go the Other Way
articles.byline: Kaia Brightwater, The Florida Atlantic Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Tulsa Golden Hurricane (6-4) 38, Florida Atlantic Owls (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa. Next: vs South Florida, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton
articles.text:
Owl fans, I flew to Tulsa thinking we were going to steal one. Tulsa 38, Florida Atlantic 21. The Golden Hurricane got us at H. A. Chapman Stadium, and our record slips to 6-4. We moved the ball. We just couldn't stop the long ones.

Caden Veltkamp completed 32 of 58 throws for 340 yards and two touchdowns. He found Easton Messer for 7 yards in the second quarter and Kelby Valsin for 2 yards right at the start of the fourth to make it 31-21. Valsin caught 10 balls for 94 yards. AJ Johnson had a 28-yard catch, and Tucker Holloway had a 27-yarder. Brady Tillman III ran in from 6 yards. We finished with 422 yards. That's plenty of offense on any Saturday.

The problem was the other side of the ball, and also the downs. We went 5 of 25 on third down and 7 of 13 on fourth down. That's a lot of fourth-down tries, and six of them came up empty. Then, 12 seconds after Valsin's touchdown, Tulsa ran one back 75 yards, and the comeback was gone. Earlier, they had broken a 78-yarder. Two plays, 153 yards, two touchdowns. That's the game.

The defense still made some plays. Jonathan Bax had eight tackles, 3.5 for loss and a sack. Joseph Sipp Jr. made seven stops. Tyson Rooks intercepted a throw and returned it 38 yards, and JK Johnson picked off another and ran it back 34. D. Rogers Jr. also recovered a fumble in the second quarter.

Six and four is still a good season, and this team isn't done. We're already bowl eligible, and there's plenty left to play for in Boca.

A home Saturday in Boca. Let's answer this, Owls. The Florida Atlantic Owls host South Florida at Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Tulsa vs Florida Atlantic: Big Plays and Six Wins on a Loud Night in Chapman
articles.matchup: Final: Tulsa Golden Hurricane (6-4) 38, Florida Atlantic Owls (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa. Next: vs Charlotte, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa
articles.text:
Hurricane fans, we are going bowling. Tulsa 38, Florida Atlantic 21. The Golden Hurricane got us at H. A. Chapman Stadium, and our record slips to 6-4. I have been waiting all season to write that sentence, and I am going to enjoy it.

The big plays were ridiculous, in the best way. Trequan Jones broke a 78-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, less than a minute after FAU had scored, and then punched in a 2-yarder in the third. Damari Alston, 14 seconds into the fourth quarter, took a handoff and went 75 yards to the house right after FAU had cut it to 31-21. Two long scoring runs that had Chapman bouncing. Alston finished with 92 yards, and Jones had 88.

Baylor Hayes threw for 309 yards and two touchdowns, both to Jimmy Calloway, from 5 yards late in the first quarter and 9 yards early in the second. We never trailed. Javon Ross was spectacular, with six catches for 163 yards, including a 41-yarder. Oran Singleton Jr. had seven grabs. Owen Carey added a 41-yard field goal.

The defense had to work, because FAU threw it 63 times. Rylan Leathers made 13 tackles, broke up two throws and had a tackle for loss. Chris Thompson Jr. made nine stops. Thomas Davis had a sack and a half, and Zach Williams intercepted a throw in the fourth quarter. We did throw two interceptions and lose a fumble, so it wasn't clean. But we finished with 501 yards, and that's how you become bowl eligible.

Six and four. Chapman was loud, and I was louder. This group has had its ups and downs, but it found a way, and now we get bonus football in December.

Let's keep this going. Go Hurricane! The Tulsa Golden Hurricane host Charlotte at H. A. Chapman Stadium, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: North Carolina vs Louisville: Benjamin Hall Scores Twice, but a Late Bounce Goes the Wrong Way
articles.byline: Ainsley Pemberton, The North Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville Cardinals (7-3) 16, North Carolina Tar Heels (5-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill. Next: at Virginia, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:30 PM ET, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville
articles.text:
Tar Heel fans, I'm sick about this one. Louisville 16, North Carolina 14. That was Saturday night at Kenan Stadium. It leaves us at 5-5. We had the ball, down two, with a chance to win it in the final minute. And then a fourth-down throw bounced off our receiver's hands and into theirs.

Benjamin Hall was our best player. He ran in an 11-yard touchdown in the first quarter, and with 3:43 left, he punched in a 6-yarder to make it 16-14. Kenan was rocking. Then our defense got a stop and gave us one more chance. With 58 seconds left, on fourth down, the ball ricocheted off Jordan Shipp and Louisville picked it off. I just put my head in my hands.

Shipp still had a strong night, with seven catches for 61 yards. Jelani Thurman caught five balls for 72 yards, including a 34-yarder. Billy Edwards Jr. went 10 of 14 for 120 yards, and Travis Burgess ran for 35 yards and threw for 59. Demon June ran for 44.

The defense kept us in it. Derek McDonald made 11 tackles. Greg Smith III had a sack and two tackles for loss. Jaiden Patterson made seven stops, and Kaleb Cost had six. Louisville scored one touchdown all night, and it came after a fumble at our 21.

But we left points on the board. Rece Verhoff missed a 39-yard field goal in the third quarter, and we came up short on fourth down at the Louisville 18 early in the fourth. Two points. That's all it was.

And after the final kneel-down, things got out of hand, and players had to be separated. Nobody wants that. Let's put it behind us.

Big one, Heels. The North Carolina Tar Heels travel to face Virginia in Charlottesville, Nov. 21, 12:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Louisville vs North Carolina: Jabari Mack's Late Interception Makes It Five Straight
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville Cardinals (7-3) 16, North Carolina Tar Heels (5-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill. Next: vs Pittsburgh, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville
articles.text:
Card Nation, my heart is racing. Louisville 16, North Carolina 14 on Saturday night at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, and we're 7-3 with five straight wins. I've never been so happy to see a ball bounce off somebody's hands.

Here's the moment. UNC had just scored with 3:43 left to make it 16-14, and they got the ball back with a chance to win. On fourth down, with 58 seconds left, their throw ricocheted off a receiver, and Jabari Mack snatched it. He ran it back 32 yards and slid down to keep the clock moving. Smart, smart player. We knelt it out from there.

Carson Hilbert was huge. Field goals of 46, 32 and 36 yards. That 36-yarder midway through the fourth quarter gave us a 16-7 lead, and we needed every point. Lincoln Kienholz completed 23 of 31 throws for 154 yards and found Jaleel Skinner for a 3-yard touchdown early in the second quarter. Lawayne McCoy caught six balls for 64 yards. Keyjuan Brown ran for 78 and Isaac Brown for 59.

The defense set that touchdown up. Koen Entringer sacked Billy Edwards Jr. and forced a fumble, and J. Donald recovered at the UNC 21. A couple of minutes later, Skinner was in the end zone. Entringer finished with two sacks. Stanquan Clark had 10 tackles and a sack, and Clev Lubin added another. J. Smith II broke up a fourth-down throw early in the fourth.

Things got heated after the final kneel-down, and players had to be separated. That's not how anybody wants a game to end. I'd rather remember the interception.

Seven and three. Five in a row. Let's keep it going at home. I've been waiting all year for a November like this one.

Go Cards! The Louisville Cardinals host Pittsburgh at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Minnesota vs Penn State: Javon Tracy Scores Twice on a Cold Night in Happy Valley
articles.matchup: Final: Penn State Nittany Lions (6-4) 42, Minnesota Golden Gophers (5-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Beaver Stadium, University Park. Next: vs Northwestern, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
Gopher fans, I thought the flurries would feel like home. They didn't help. Penn State 42, Minnesota 14 on Saturday at Beaver Stadium, and we're 5-5. More than 105,000 people were there, and most of them were celebrating by halftime.

It went sideways right away. Drake Lindsey fumbled on our first drive, Penn State recovered at our 44, and they scored a few plays later. It was 14-0 after one quarter and 28-0 at halftime. They ran for 173 yards in the first half alone. We just couldn't get off the field.

But I want to give Javon Tracy his flowers. Down 35-0 in the third quarter, he caught a 10-yard touchdown from Lindsey, then a 15-yarder a few minutes later. Two scores in less than five minutes, and our little corner of the stadium got loud. Tracy finished with six catches for 51 yards. Darius Taylor had a 58-yard catch and four grabs for 85 yards. Lindsey threw for 185 yards and both touchdowns.

Maverick Baranowski was a warrior on defense with 11 tackles and a sack. Joey Gerlach had a sack and eight tackles. Matt Kingsbury made six stops, and Kerry Brown and TJ Bush Jr. each made five. They kept swinging the whole night.

We ran for 41 yards. You can't win a Big Ten road game like that, and we didn't. We converted 3 of 4 on fourth down, but the one we missed came early in the fourth quarter with a chance to make it closer.

Five and five, with two to go. One more and we're bowl eligible. This team has bounced back before, and I fully expect it to bounce back again. Let's get it at home this Saturday.

Ski-U-Mah! The Minnesota Golden Gophers host Northwestern at Huntington Bank Stadium, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Penn State vs Minnesota: Becht, Hansen and a Snowy Beaver Stadium Make Six
articles.byline: Luann Kessler, The Penn State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Penn State Nittany Lions (6-4) 42, Minnesota Golden Gophers (5-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Beaver Stadium, University Park. Next: vs Rutgers, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Beaver Stadium, University Park
articles.text:
We Are! Penn State 42, Minnesota 14 on Saturday at Beaver Stadium, and we're 6-4 and bowl eligible. More than 105,000 of us stood in mist and flurries and watched this team look like a team. Three straight Big Ten wins. I'm thawing out with a smile on my face.

Rocco Becht ran for one touchdown and threw for three. He snuck in from 1 yard in the first quarter, then found Benjamin Brahmer for 19 yards a few minutes later. Late in the second, he hit Cam Wallace for a 1-yard score, and early in the third, he found Brahmer again from 4 yards. Two touchdown catches for Brahmer. That's my guy.

And the ground game set the tone. Carson Hansen ran 12 times for 126 yards, including a 46-yard touchdown run early in the second quarter that had the student section losing it. Cam Wallace added 82 yards on 15 carries. We ran for 229 yards, and 173 of them came in the first half. Alex Manske even came in late and threw a 22-yard touchdown to James Peoples.

The defense smothered Minnesota early. Kooper Ebel recovered a fumble on their first drive and made nine tackles. Alexander McPherson had a sack and two tackles for loss. Tony Rojas had a tackle and a half for loss. Cam Smith made eight tackles. Minnesota ran for 41 yards all day, and it was 35-0 before they scored.

Coach Matt Campbell said this group had to become a team and find its identity. After that four-game skid to start Big Ten play, I wasn't sure. Now I am. This is a team.

Six and four. Bowl bound. Let's finish strong.

Bundle up and bring the noise. We Are! The Penn State Nittany Lions host Rutgers at Beaver Stadium, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: San Jose State vs Air Force: The Spartans Can't Slow the Falcon Ground Game
articles.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, The San José State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force Falcons (8-2) 24, San José State Spartans (5-6) 3, Sat., Nov. 14, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy. Next: vs UNLV, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:00 PM ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose
articles.text:
Spartan fans, that one was a grind, and not the good kind. Air Force 24, San Jose State 3. That was Saturday night at Falcon Stadium. It leaves us at 5-6. We're one win away from a bowl, and we get one more chance at home.

Air Force ran the ball 72 times for 452 yards. They didn't complete a single throw all night, and they didn't need to. We held them scoreless in the first quarter, and for a while it looked like our defense was going to make this a fight. Then the second quarter came, and they scored 17 points, including an 81-yard touchdown run with 1:56 left before halftime.

Our defense still played its heart out. Naseri Danielson made 13 tackles. Dylan Lee and Ethan Powell each had nine, and Lee added a sack. Powell had a tackle and a half for loss. Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa made eight stops, and Dejon Roney had seven. Air Force went 2 of 5 on fourth down, and we forced a fumble in the first quarter. Those guys were on the field for more than 39 minutes, at altitude, and they never stopped.

The offense never found a rhythm. Luke Weaver completed 11 of 24 throws for 138 yards. Carson Clark caught six balls for 57 yards. Jabari Bates had a 39-yard catch, and Jase Nix had a 31-yarder. Trajan Sinatra made a 33-yard field goal early in the third quarter, but he missed a 37-yarder later. We went 2 of 12 on third down and didn't give it away, but we just didn't have the ball enough.

This one hurts. But the bowl hopes come down to one Saturday now, and I'll be there.

Bowl game on the table. Let's go, Spartans! The San José State Spartans host UNLV at CEFCU Stadium, Nov. 21, 7 PM ET.

articles.title: Air Force vs San Jose State: 452 Rushing Yards and Zero Completions Needed
articles.byline: Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, The Air Force Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force Falcons (8-2) 24, San José State Spartans (5-6) 3, Sat., Nov. 14, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy. Next: vs UTEP, Fri., Nov. 20, 8:00 PM ET, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy
articles.text:
Falcon fans, that's Air Force football in its purest form. Air Force 24, San Jose State 3 on Saturday night at Falcon Stadium, and we're 8-2. We threw the ball five times. We completed none of them. We won by 21. I love this team so much.

We ran the ball 72 times for 452 yards. Seventy-two! Evan Medders carried 13 times for 146 yards, and with 1:56 left in the first half, he broke an 81-yard touchdown run that had me sprinting down the aisle like I was the one carrying it. Kemper Hodges ran 26 times for 117 yards and two touchdowns, a 4-yarder to finish an 80-yard drive in the second quarter and a 7-yarder late in the fourth. Owen Allen added 103 yards on 12 carries, including a 54-yard burst.

The first quarter was scoreless, and I'll admit I was a little nervous. We came up short on a fourth down and lost a fumble. But then the second quarter happened. Carter Cremascoli hit a 38-yard field goal, Hodges scored, Medders went the distance, and it was 17-0 at the break.

The defense was terrific all night. San Jose State managed 224 yards and went 2 of 12 on third down. Blake Fletcher made eight tackles and stuffed a fourth-down run in the fourth quarter. Roger Jones Jr. had six solo tackles. Korey Johnson and Dallas Daley each had a tackle for loss and a hurry. The Spartans' only points came on a 33-yard field goal early in the third, and they missed another later.

We held the ball for more than 39 minutes. Their offense barely got a turn.

Eight and two. This is a special group, and Falcon Stadium knows it.

A Friday night at home. Fly, Fight, Win! The Air Force Falcons host UTEP at Falcon Stadium, Friday, Nov. 20, 8 PM ET.

articles.title: Troy vs South Alabama: Goose Crowder Fights, but Two Long Runs Sink the Trojans
articles.matchup: Final: South Alabama Jaguars (5-5) 27, Troy Trojans (4-6) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile. Next: vs Georgia Southern, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL), Troy
articles.text:
Trojan fans, I don't love writing these. South Alabama 27, Troy 14. That was Saturday night at Hancock Whitney Stadium in Mobile. It leaves us at 4-6. Two long runs in the first quarter put us in a hole, and we never climbed out.

The first one came 1:23 into the game, a 46-yard touchdown run. The second came with 37 seconds left in the first quarter, a 44-yarder. By the time I'd finished my hot dog, we were down 14-0. Their running back finished with 153 yards on 14 carries. We just couldn't get him on the ground.

But Goose Crowder never quit. Early in the second quarter, he took off on a 45-yard touchdown run that got our whole section on its feet. 14-7. And early in the fourth, he found Nick Hampton for a 4-yard touchdown. Crowder finished 24 of 41 for 231 yards and ran for 58 more. Noreel White caught four balls for 55 yards, Jordan Lovett had six grabs and Mojo Dortch had four.

We didn't give it away once, and we held the ball for more than 32 minutes. But we went 5 of 17 on third down, and we came up short on fourth down three times, including a throw into the end zone late in the fourth. Nine penalties for 95 yards didn't help either. Too many drives ended a few yards short.

Justin Powe made nine tackles and broke up two throws. Keno Jones had seven stops, and Jamarion Keyes made six. TJ Thompson and Miquon Merriweather each had a piece of a tackle for loss.

Four and six. It's been a tough year, but this team still plays hard, and I'm still proud to wear the cardinal.

Back home in Troy. Go Trojans! The Troy Trojans host Georgia Southern at Veterans Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET.

articles.title: South Alabama vs Troy: Trae'von Dunbar Breaks Two Long Runs, and the Jaguars Snap the Skid
articles.byline: Azalea Fairhope-Grice, The South Alabama Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Alabama Jaguars (5-5) 27, Troy Trojans (4-6) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile. Next: at Southern Miss, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg
articles.text:
Jag fans, we needed that one badly. South Alabama 27, Troy 14 on Saturday night at Hancock Whitney Stadium in Mobile, and we're 5-5. Three straight losses, gone. And we beat Troy to do it. That's a good Saturday in Mobile.

Trae'von Dunbar was electric. On our first drive, 1:23 into the game, he broke a 46-yard touchdown run. With 37 seconds left in the first quarter, he went 44 yards for another. Fourteen carries, 153 yards, two touchdowns. Every time he touched the ball, I stood up.

Bishop Davenport added a 28-yard touchdown run in the third quarter that made it 27-7. He threw for 122 yards, including a 46-yard strike to Trae Stevenson. PJ Martin ran 17 times for 50 yards and did the dirty work. Dylan Freebury made field goals of 29 and 24 yards. We ran for 246 yards and didn't give it away once.

The defense was the other hero. Camen Upshaw made 11 tackles, and he stuffed a fourth-down run in the first quarter. Jordan Williams had 10 tackles and a sack. Seidrion Langston had 10 more. Jaylen Moson broke up two throws, including a fourth-down throw in the third quarter. Troy went for it six times on fourth down, and we stopped them three times, including a throw into our end zone late in the fourth quarter.

Troy did get a 45-yard touchdown run from its quarterback, and they scored again early in the fourth. But that was it. When it mattered, we held.

Five and five. Bowl eligibility is one win away. I believe. This team has had a tough stretch, but tonight it looked like the group I watched in September, fast and hungry and having fun.

Let's go get number six, Jags! The South Alabama Jaguars travel to face Southern Miss in Hattiesburg, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET.

articles.title: Baylor vs BYU: A Rough Night in Provo Ends a Two-Game Winning Streak
articles.matchup: Final: BYU Cougars (8-2) 28, Baylor Bears (6-4) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo. Next: vs Texas Tech, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, McLane Stadium, Waco
articles.text:
Baylor Nation, I flew to Utah full of hope, and I'm flying home a little quieter. BYU 28, Baylor 7. That was Saturday night at LaVell Edwards Stadium. It leaves us at 6-4. Our two-game winning streak has ended. That one was a long, long night.

BYU scored touchdowns on its first three drives and led 21-0 at halftime. Their quarterback ran for three of those, and our defense just couldn't get him on the ground near the goal. They ran for 189 yards and held the ball for more than 37 minutes. Our guys were on the field a lot.

Still, the defense had some fight. Travion Barnes made 10 tackles and one for loss. Kyland Reed had eight and a tackle for loss. Micah Gifford and Devin Turner each made seven stops. They kept BYU out of the end zone for the entire third quarter and into the fourth, and that gave us a chance to make it interesting.

DJ Lagway did what he could. He completed 21 of 37 throws for 159 yards, and early in the fourth quarter, he found Matthew Klopfenstein for a 3-yard touchdown. Jadon Porter caught five balls for 50 yards, and Gavin Freeman had six grabs. We converted 9 of 16 on third down, which is pretty good. But we finished with 238 yards, and we came up short on a deep fourth-down throw toward the BYU goal late in the fourth. That was our last real chance.

Nine penalties for 80 yards didn't help either. You can't do that on the road against a top-15 team.

Six and four. We're still in a good spot, and I still believe in this group.

Back home in Waco. Sic 'em, Bears! The Baylor Bears host Texas Tech at McLane Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: BYU vs Baylor: Bear Bachmeier Runs for Three, and LaVell Edwards Stays Perfect
articles.matchup: Final: BYU Cougars (8-2) 28, Baylor Bears (6-4) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo. Next: at Kansas, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence
articles.text:
Cougar fans, Provo was electric. BYU 28, Baylor 7 on Saturday night at LaVell Edwards Stadium, and we're 8-2 and 6-0 at home. The No. 12 Cougars took care of business, and I've got the blue face paint to prove it.

Bear Bachmeier was a bulldozer. He ran for three touchdowns, from 8 yards and 5 yards in the first quarter and 1 yard late in the second. Then in the fourth, he threw a 23-yard touchdown to Jojo Phillips to put it away. He finished with 158 yards of offense, and every one of them looked like it hurt the guy trying to tackle him.

We scored touchdowns on our first three drives. Three for three! The run game piled up 189 yards. LJ Martin had 49 on six carries, Sione Moa ran for 37 and Preston Rex had 28. Walker Lyons caught three balls for 49 yards. We held the ball for more than 37 minutes, and we didn't give it away once.

The defense was stifling. Baylor didn't score until the fourth quarter. Bodie Schoonover had two sacks, and Viliami Po'uha added another. Tommy Prassas intercepted a throw in the third quarter. And late in the fourth, J. Clifton hurried a deep fourth-down throw, and it fell incomplete near our goal. Keanu Tanuvasa had a tackle for loss, and Raider Damuni and Faletau Satuala each made five stops.

Matthias Dunn missed a field goal early in the fourth, which kept my blood pressure up for a minute. No big deal. He was perfect on extra points.

Eight and two. Unbeaten at home. This team is something special, and this stadium knows it. I'll be wearing blue all week, and I'll be smiling the whole time.

Rise and shout, Cougars! The BYU Cougars travel to face Kansas in Lawrence, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Kentucky vs Florida: A Second-Half Lead Gets Away at Kroger Field
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Gators (6-4) 21, Kentucky Wildcats (7-3) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Kroger Field, Lexington. Next: at Missouri, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Memorial Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Big Blue Nation, that one stings. Florida 21, Kentucky 14. That was Saturday night at Kroger Field. It leaves us at 7-3. We led 7-0 at halftime and 14-10 midway through the third. And we let it get away in front of a big home crowd.

The first half was all defense, and our defense was terrific. Kenny Minchey found CJ Baxter for a 5-yard touchdown late in the first quarter, and it was 7-0. Then a holding penalty in our own end zone gave Florida a safety before halftime. Two points for a penalty. That's the kind of thing that comes back to bite you.

Early in the third quarter, Minchey was strip-sacked at our 30, and Florida scored right after. We answered. Minchey punched it in himself from 1 yard to make it 14-10, and Kroger Field was rocking. DJ Miller caught four balls for 80 yards, and Willie Rodriguez had five for 62. Minchey finished 15 of 26 for 181 yards.

But we only ran for 61 yards, and Florida ran for 211. They held the ball for more than 34 minutes and kept chipping away. A field goal made it 14-13, and with 9:08 left, their quarterback ran one in from 2 yards. They added the two-point try, and it was 21-14.

We had two chances. With 5:34 left, we came up short on fourth down at the Florida 8. Then, after our defense made a fourth-down stop of its own at our 36, we got the ball back and came up short on fourth down again with 1:31 left. That's the game.

Grant Godfrey was a beast with 13 tackles. Elijah Barnes made nine, and Jordan Castell made eight. Lorenzo Cowan had a sack, and T. Gadson made the fourth-down stop. This defense deserved better.

Seven and three is still a great season. Let's finish it right.

Go Cats! The Kentucky Wildcats travel to face Missouri in Columbia, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Florida vs Kentucky: Aaron Philo Comes Back and Leads the Gators to a Bowl
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Gators (6-4) 21, Kentucky Wildcats (7-3) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Kroger Field, Lexington. Next: vs Vanderbilt, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville
articles.text:
Gator Nation, chomp chomp! Florida 21, Kentucky 14 on Saturday night at Kroger Field in Lexington, and we're 6-4 and bowl eligible. We went on the road, beat the No. 13 team in the country, and came from behind to do it. What a night.

Aaron Philo is the story. Two weeks ago he was benched against Georgia. On Saturday he was back as the starter, and he played like a man with something to prove. He threw for 119 yards and ran for 102 more, and with 9:08 left, he ran it in from 2 yards for the go-ahead score. Kahleil Jackson then found Dallas Wilson for the two-point conversion, and it was 21-14. Coach Jon Sumrall said Philo didn't hang his head last weekend and ran with toughness and physicality. I agree with every word.

Jadan Baugh scored his SEC-leading 15th touchdown on a 1-yard run in the third quarter, and Philo ran in the two-point try himself. Patrick Durkin hit a 37-yard field goal. We ran for 211 yards, held the ball for more than 34 minutes and didn't give it away once.

And the defense? Outstanding. Jayden Woods had a sack and a half, including a strip-sack early in the third quarter that B. Bett recovered at the Kentucky 30. Myles Graham had a half sack. Kentucky's holding penalty in the end zone gave us a safety before halftime. Then, with everything at stake, we stopped them twice on fourth down. Aaron Chiles hurried a throw at our 8 with 5:34 left, and Ben Hanks III broke up the last one with 1:31 to go. Hanks and Chiles each made seven tackles.

Six wins. A road win against a top-15 team. A quarterback who fought his way back. I'm going to sleep well tonight.

Let's fill The Swamp. Go Gators! The Florida Gators host Vanderbilt at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Marshall vs App State: A 13-3 Lead Slips Away in Huntington
articles.matchup: Final: App State Mountaineers (6-4) 20, Marshall Thundering Herd (5-5) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington. Next: vs Georgia State, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington
articles.text:
Herd fans, I've been staring at the ceiling for an hour. App State 20, Marshall 16. Our record at Joan C. Edwards Stadium took a hit, and we're 5-5. We led 13-3 in the second quarter, and we couldn't hold on.

The first half was a lot of fun. Freshman Jorge Diaz Nicolas was perfect. He kicked field goals of 31, 54 and 24 yards. That 54-yarder early in the second quarter had the whole stadium roaring. Then Kelvon McBride strip-sacked their quarterback, Cole Funderburk recovered it, and four plays later TJ Lester ran it in from 2 yards. 13-3, and Huntington was rocking.

Daytione Smith intercepted a throw in the first quarter. Mekhi Lockhart had a sack. Kenyatta Hardge and Caleb Clark-Glover each made eight tackles, and Funderburk forced a fumble at our 16 in the fourth quarter that C. McCartherens recovered. The defense gave us plenty of chances.

Jo'Shon Barbie ran 17 times for 108 yards. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson ran for 66 more. We ran for 210 yards and held the ball for more than 34 minutes. But we went 1 of 4 on fourth down, and that's the story. Late in the fourth quarter, our punter, Cooper Heimbach, threw a 25-yard strike to Sherone White Jr. on a fake. Six plays later, Barbie was stopped for no gain on fourth-and-1, and App State got the ball at its 19 with 3:11 left. We got one more chance and came up empty on fourth down again. Earlier in the fourth, we'd been stopped on fourth down at our own 34 too.

App State's 37-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter was the play that beat us. One play. That's how close this was.

Five and five, with two to go. I still believe this team gets to a bowl, and I'll be in my seat to watch them do it.

Back home, back to work. We Are... Marshall! The Marshall Thundering Herd host Georgia State at Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET.

articles.title: App State vs Marshall: Henry Hasselbeck's 37-Yard Run Makes the Mountaineers Bowl Eligible
articles.byline: Zebulon 'Zeb' Coldiron, The App State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: App State Mountaineers (6-4) 20, Marshall Thundering Herd (5-5) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington. Next: vs UL Monroe, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone
articles.text:
Mountaineer fans, grab the black and gold and dance. App State 20, Marshall 16 on Saturday at Joan C. Edwards Stadium in Huntington, and we're 6-4 and bowl eligible. Down 13-3 in the second quarter, and we came back to win it on the road. Yosef would be proud.

Henry Hasselbeck was the man. He scored twice on the ground. The first was a 1-yard run in the third quarter that tied it 13-13. The second was a beauty. Early in the fourth, on third-and-1, he took off and went 37 yards to the house to finish a seven-play, 71-yard drive, and we led 20-16 with 12:55 left. I screamed so loud my dog left the room.

Jaquari Lewis carried us too. Twenty-three carries, 137 yards, and he never stopped churning. Sam Pickett III caught five balls for 89 yards. James London kicked two 31-yard field goals, including one as the first half ended to make it 13-6.

Then it was up to the defense, and the defense delivered. Marshall faked a punt and gained 25 yards, but six plays later, we stopped Jo'Shon Barbie for no gain on fourth-and-1 with 3:11 left. Then a couple of minutes later, we got them on fourth down again. J. Brown hurried the throw, and it fell incomplete. Ballgame.

Carson Sloan made 13 tackles. Colton Phares had 12 and forced a fumble that R. Lolohea recovered. Ja'Den McBurrows and Aaron Clark each made eight stops. Marshall went 1 of 4 on fourth down, and that was the difference.

We did have three turnovers. That's something to clean up. But six wins is six wins, and we're going bowling. Somebody start planning the road trip.

Let's pack The Rock in Boone. Go Apps! The App State Mountaineers host UL Monroe at Kidd Brewer Stadium, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Oregon State vs Boise State: Maalik Murphy Throws for 396, and the Beavers Push the Broncos to the End
articles.byline: Juniper Ostrowski, The Oregon State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Boise State Broncos (9-1) 46, Oregon State Beavers (5-5) 41, Sat., Nov. 14, Albertsons Stadium, Boise. Next: vs Utah State, Sat., Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET, Reser Stadium, Corvallis
articles.text:
Beaver Nation, I'm proud of this team, and I'm heartbroken at the same time. Boise State 46, Oregon State 41. That was Saturday night at Albertsons Stadium. It leaves us at 5-5. We went into the loudest place in the league, with College GameDay in town, and traded punches with a 9-1 team for four quarters.

Maalik Murphy was phenomenal. He completed 31 of 39 throws for 396 yards and three touchdowns. Jesse Legree caught 12 balls for 140 yards and a 15-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Adonis McDaniel had a 40-yard catch. Eric Olsen caught a 20-yard touchdown with 4:25 left to make it 46-41, and Cynai Thomas grabbed a 12-yarder in the fourth quarter. Every time Boise State scored, we came right back.

Jake Reichle punched in two short touchdowns, from 1 and 5 yards. Cornell Hatcher Jr. ran in from 2 yards. We converted 6 of 9 on third down and finished with 506 yards. That's an offense that can play with anybody.

There were a few that got away. Late in the first quarter, Boise State returned an interception 58 yards for a touchdown and added a two-point conversion to go up 15-7. Caleb Ojeda missed a field goal earlier in that quarter. And Rasean Jones caught 11 balls for 230 yards against us. We just couldn't stop that guy.

Aiden Sullivan was a monster on defense, with 12 tackles and a sack. Jaheim Patterson and Gyriece Goodman each made seven tackles. Drake Vickers broke up two throws. After Olsen's touchdown, Boise State got the ball back and ran out the clock, and we never got another chance.

Five and five. This team is close to something good.

Bring the orange to Corvallis. Go Beavs! The Oregon State Beavers host Utah State at Reser Stadium, Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Boise State vs Oregon State: Rasean Jones Goes for 230, and the Broncos Will Host the Title Game
articles.byline: Thatcher Bluestem, The Boise State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Boise State Broncos (9-1) 46, Oregon State Beavers (5-5) 41, Sat., Nov. 14, Albertsons Stadium, Boise. Next: vs San Diego State, Sat., Nov. 21, 9:30 PM ET, Albertsons Stadium, Boise
articles.text:
Bronco Nation, we did it. Boise State 46, Oregon State 41 on Saturday night at Albertsons Stadium, and we're 9-1, 6-0 in the Pac-12, with nine straight wins. And we will host the Pac-12 championship game on Dec. 4. On the blue turf. In front of us. I've been yelling since the final kneel-down.

College GameDay came to town, and some of us camped out overnight to be part of the show. My feet are numb, and I would do it again tomorrow.

Rasean Jones was unbelievable. Eleven catches, 230 yards and three touchdowns, from 19, 16 and 26 yards. Coach Spencer Danielson said it was one of the best performances he's seen from a receiver in his 10 years here, and that every catch and every yard was needed. He's right. Oregon State kept answering, and Jones kept answering back.

Maddux Madsen came back after missing the previous game and was brilliant. Twenty-three of 32 for a career-best 371 yards and four touchdowns. Jones said it was great to have Mad Dog back. Matt Wagner caught a 9-yard score early in the fourth and a two-point conversion too. Sire Gaines ran in from 4 yards. Canaan Moore kicked a 38-yard field goal right before halftime.

And the play that flipped the first quarter? Travis Anderson stepped in front of a throw and took it back 58 yards for a touchdown. That made it 15-7, and the stadium was shaking. Anderson finished with eight tackles too. Jaden Mickey made seven stops.

It got close at the end. Oregon State scored with 4:25 left to make it 46-41. But we got the ball back and ran out the clock. Kneel-downs never felt so good.

One more at home before the big one. Go Broncos! The Boise State Broncos host San Diego State at Albertsons Stadium, Nov. 21, 9:30 PM ET.

And we will host the Pac-12 championship game on Dec. 4. On the blue turf. In front of us. I've been yelling since the final kneel-down.
College GameDay came to town, and some of us camped out overnight to be part of the show. My feet are numb, and I would do it again tomorrow.

Rasean Jones was unbelievable. Eleven catches, 230 yards and three touchdowns, from 19, 16 and 26 yards. Coach Spencer Danielson said it was one of the best performances he's seen from a receiver in his 10 years here, and that every catch and every yard was needed. He's right. Oregon State kept answering, and Jones kept answering back.

Maddux Madsen came back after missing the previous game and was brilliant. Twenty-three of 32 for a career-best 371 yards and four touchdowns. Jones said it was great to have Mad Dog back. Matt Wagner caught a 9-yard score early in the fourth and a two-point conversion too. Sire Gaines ran in from 4 yards. Canaan Moore kicked a 38-yard field goal right before halftime.

articles.title: Michigan State vs Washington: Tied Late, Then a Tough Finish in East Lansing
articles.byline: Shay Kowalczyk, The Michigan State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Huskies (6-4) 21, Michigan State Spartans (3-7) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing. Next: vs Oregon, Fri., Nov. 20, 8:00 PM ET, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing
articles.text:
Spartan fans, this one hurts. Washington 21, Michigan State 14. That was Saturday night at Spartan Stadium. It leaves us at 3-7. It was tied 14-14 from late in the second quarter all the way to 2:24 left. We had our chances, and we just couldn't grab one.

The start was great. Carson Gulker ran it in from 1 yard in the first quarter, and the student section was bouncing. Washington tied it late in the first quarter on a 58-yard throw, then went ahead in the second. We answered before halftime when Cam Fancher found Bryson Williams for a 2-yard touchdown. 14-14 at the break, and the place was loud.

Brandon Tullis ran 21 times for 82 yards. Fredrick Moore caught four balls for 66 yards, and Williams caught four for 63. Alessio Milivojevic came in and went 7 of 12 for 108 yards. We converted all three of our fourth-down tries, too. We moved the ball, and we held it for more than 32 minutes.

But the second half slipped away a little at a time. We threw an interception in the third quarter. Liam Boyd missed a field goal in the fourth. Then Washington drove 78 yards and scored with 2:24 left. We got one last drive into their territory, and with 35 seconds left, the ball came loose after a catch, and Washington recovered. That was it.

Nikai Martinez made five tackles, and Aveon Grose, Michael Richard and Dion Crawford each had a piece of a tackle for loss. The defense held Washington to 44 rushing yards. That deserved better.

Three and seven in Pat Fitzgerald's first season is not what any of us wanted. A bowl is off the table now. But I'm not going anywhere, and neither are the people sitting next to me.

A Friday night at home. Let's make some noise, Spartans! The Michigan State Spartans host Oregon at Spartan Stadium, Friday, Nov. 20, 8 PM ET.

articles.title: Washington vs Michigan State: A Wild Travel Day, a Late Jayden Limar Score and Six Wins
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Huskies (6-4) 21, Michigan State Spartans (3-7) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing. Next: vs Indiana, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Husky Stadium, Seattle
articles.text:
Dawg Pack, what a day. Washington 21, Michigan State 14 on Saturday night at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, and we're 6-4 and headed to a bowl game. The federal flight grounding scrambled our travel, and the team arrived about 15 hours before kickoff. They didn't care. They came to play.

Coach Jedd Fisch said there was a lot of adversity during the last 24 hours and the team handled it exceptionally well. Demond Williams Jr. said they knew the game was getting played no matter when they flew in. I love that attitude. I was refreshing the flight tracker all Friday night, and these guys just showed up and went to work.

Chris Lawson was spectacular. Five catches, 124 yards and two touchdowns. The first was a 58-yarder late in the first quarter to tie it 7-7. The second was a 17-yarder in the second quarter. Williams finished 22 of 33 for 288 yards and two scores, and Decker DeGraaf added a 33-yard grab.

It was 14-14 for the whole second half until the very end. Then we went 78 yards in eight plays. Williams hit Lawson deep for 21 yards to the 1, and Jayden Limar plunged in with 2:24 left. I jumped so high I nearly hit the ceiling of my living room.

The defense finished it. Michigan State had one last drive into our territory, and with 35 seconds left, Xe'ree Alexander knocked the ball loose, and D. Colman-Brusa fell on it. Jacob Manu intercepted a throw in the third quarter and made eight tackles. Alex McLaughlin had 10 tackles and broke up two throws. Jacob Lane added a tackle and a half for loss.

Three straight road wins. Six wins. Bowl eligible. This was a gritty one, and I'm so proud.

Purple Reign, Seattle. Bow down to Washington! The Washington Huskies host Indiana at Husky Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: UCF vs Arizona State: Josh Derry Shines, but the Knights Can't Catch Up
articles.matchup: Final: Arizona State Sun Devils (6-4) 26, UCF Knights (5-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando. Next: vs Iowa State, Fri., Nov. 20, 6:00 PM ET, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando
articles.text:
Knight fans, the Bounce House never stopped trying. Arizona State 26, UCF 13. That was Saturday at the Acrisure Bounce House. It leaves us at 5-5. We needed one more win to get bowl eligible, and we're still waiting on it.

The second quarter is where it got away. Arizona State scored five seconds into the quarter, and Will Stone missed a 34-yard field goal a few minutes later. We finally got on the board when Landen Chambers ran it in from 2 yards with 1:53 left before halftime, and it was 10-7. The place got loud again. Then Alonza Barnett III lost a fumble at our 19, and Arizona State kicked two field goals in the last 43 seconds of the half. 16-7 at the break.

Josh Derry was terrific. Seven catches for 137 yards, including a 46-yarder that got the whole place up. Barnett completed 21 of 30 throws for 257 yards, and late in the fourth, he hit Tyren Hornes for a 40-yard touchdown. Hornes finished with five catches for 59 yards. Chambers ran for 54 on seven carries.

But we only ran the ball 23 times. Arizona State held it for more than 37 minutes, and we came up short on fourth down twice in the fourth quarter. Our defense still fought hard. Caleb Flagg and Tackett Curtis each made eight tackles. Antione Jackson broke up three throws, and Jayden Williams had a tackle for loss. Isaiah Nixon made six stops.

Five and five, with two to play. I'm not panicking, and neither should you. This team has been good at home, and the next one is at home. One more, Knights. That's all we need.

A Friday night at home. Let's bring the noise. Charge On! The UCF Knights host Iowa State at Acrisure Bounce House, Friday, Nov. 20, 6 PM ET.

articles.title: Arizona State vs UCF: Carson Smith Kicks Four, and the Sun Devils Reach Six
articles.byline: Skylar Vanterpool, The Arizona State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Arizona State Sun Devils (6-4) 26, UCF Knights (5-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando. Next: vs Oklahoma State, Sat., Nov. 21, 10:15 PM ET, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe
articles.text:
Sun Devil fans, we went to Orlando and took care of business. Arizona State 26, UCF 13 on Saturday at the Acrisure Bounce House, and we're 6-4. Six wins. Bowl eligible. I'm writing this with a sunburn and a smile.

Carson Smith was the hero. Four field goals, four makes: 51 yards, 41 yards, 28 yards and 37 yards. The 51-yarder in the second quarter had our little section of the stadium on its feet. Then he hit two more in the final 43 seconds before halftime, the second one right after A. Smith III recovered a fumble at the UCF 19. We went into the locker room up 16-7, and I finally sat down.

Cardae Mack carried the load. Twenty-five carries, 111 yards and an 8-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter that made it 23-7. Marquis Gillis scored from 1 yard five seconds into the second quarter. Jake Fette completed 21 of 36 throws for 196 yards and didn't give it away once. Reed Harris caught seven balls for 80 yards. We held the ball for more than 37 minutes, converted 10 of 19 on third down and had zero turnovers. That's how you win on the road.

The defense bent and never broke until the final minutes. UCF ran for 54 yards. Martell Hughes sacked Alonza Barnett III on fourth down early in the fourth quarter. We stopped them on another fourth down a few minutes later. Owen Long made nine tackles, and Montana Warren had seven. UCF missed a field goal, and their only touchdowns came on a 2-yard run and a 40-yard throw with 2:12 left.

Six and four, with a home game next. This team keeps finding ways.

Late night in Tempe. Fork 'em, Devils! The Arizona State Sun Devils host Oklahoma State at Mountain America Stadium, Nov. 21, 10:15 PM ET.

articles.title: Southern Miss vs Louisiana Tech: Mario Sanders Shines on a Rough Night in Ruston
articles.byline: Delphine 'Dee' Broussard, The Southern Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (8-2) 63, Southern Miss Golden Eagles (3-7) 31, Sat., Nov. 14, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston. Next: vs South Alabama, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg
articles.text:
Golden Eagle fans, I'm going to be honest with you. Louisiana Tech 63, Southern Miss 31. That was Saturday night at Joe Aillet Stadium. It leaves us at 3-7. We threw an interception on the first play of the game, and the night never really got better from there.

It was 21-3 after one quarter. Then, in a two-minute stretch of the second, Louisiana Tech returned two interceptions for touchdowns, one for 36 yards and one for 89. By halftime it was 42-10. We threw four interceptions in all, and two of them went the other way for scores. You can't win like that against anybody, let alone a team that's 8-2.

There were moments worth cheering, and I cheered every one. Jamarice Wilder broke a 53-yard touchdown run early in the second quarter. Mario Sanders was outstanding, with eight catches for 119 yards, including a 41-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. Grant Page caught a 7-yard touchdown in the third. Steven Robinson ran for 94 yards, and Creighton Wilbanks hit a 44-yard field goal. And late in the fourth, MaLik Caswell intercepted a throw and took it 32 yards to the house. That one felt good.

Wesley Edison was everywhere on defense with 10 tackles and two throws broken up. Mathis Haygood made seven stops, and Landon Sylvie added five. We ran for 186 yards and finished with 406. That's not nothing. It just doesn't matter much when you hand the other team the ball five times.

Three and seven hurts. I've been coming to games since I was a kid, and I've seen this program climb out of tough spots before. But Hattiesburg is home, and home is where we fix this.

articles.title: Louisiana Tech vs Southern Miss: Two Defensive Touchdowns and a 63-Point Party in Ruston
articles.byline: Booker 'Champ' Tullos, The Louisiana Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (8-2) 63, Southern Miss Golden Eagles (3-7) 31, Sat., Nov. 14, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston. Next: vs Arkansas State, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:00 PM ET, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston
articles.text:
Bulldog fans, I need a nap. Louisiana Tech 63, Southern Miss 31 on Saturday night at Joe Aillet Stadium in Ruston, and we're 8-2, unbeaten at home and 6-0 in the Sun Belt. Joe Aillet was rocking from the first snap to the last.

And I mean the first snap. Kolbe Fields intercepted John White on the very first play from scrimmage, and four plays later Dylone Brooks ran it in from 1 yard. Then receiver Marcus Calwise Jr. threw a 49-yard touchdown to Jay Wilkerson, and I lost my mind. Sergio Snider scored from 2 yards, and it was 21-3 after one quarter.

The second quarter was even better. Blake Baker hit Talyn Shettron for a 9-yard score. Then Jadon Mayfield intercepted a throw and ran it back 36 yards for a touchdown. Less than two minutes later, Jordan McRae picked off another one at our 11 and went 89 yards the other way. Back-to-back defensive touchdowns. 42-10 at halftime. I haven't stopped grinning.

Baker finished 21 of 28 for 236 yards and three touchdowns, adding a 2-yarder to Brayden Bockler and a 12-yarder to Eli Finley. Finley caught six balls for 104 yards. Jalen Mickens had seven grabs. Rayshun Hurt broke a 55-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter and finished with 88 yards on just six carries. Kaegan Kent made all nine extra points.

The defense had four interceptions. Judd Rouyea had the other. Mayfield made nine tackles, and Alonzo Jackson Jr. had a sack and two tackles for loss. Zheric Hill had a sack too, and Taeden Rogers recovered a fumble.

Eight and two. This team is for real, and Ruston knows it. Everybody else is about to find out.

Bring your red. Go Dawgs! The Louisiana Tech Bulldogs host Arkansas State at Joe Aillet Stadium, Nov. 21, 7 PM ET.

articles.title: Rice vs Tulane: Jamir Benjamin's 62-Yard Return Wasn't Quite Enough
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane Green Wave (5-5) 20, Rice Owls (1-9) 17, Sat., Nov. 14, First Community Stadium, Houston. Next: at Temple, Thu., Nov. 19, 7:30 PM ET, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia
articles.text:
Owl fans, this one stings. Tulane 20, Rice 17. That was Saturday night at First Community Stadium. It leaves us at 1-9. We led 17-6 at halftime. We had a real chance to beat a good team in front of our own people. And it slipped away by a single fourth-down yard.

The first half was everything I wanted. Tommy Bauchiero kicked a 27-yard field goal to get us started. Gael Ochoa found Max Mosey for a 4-yard touchdown early in the second quarter. Then, with 31 seconds left before halftime, Jamir Benjamin jumped a throw at our 38 and ran it back 62 yards for a touchdown. The whole stadium was up. I was hugging people I had never met.

Our run game had Tulane on its heels. We ran 51 times for 224 yards. Ochoa ran for 82, including a 35-yard burst. D'Andre Hardeman Jr. had 66, and Davis Lane broke a 21-yarder. articles.title: Tulane vs Rice: A 2 a.m. Bus Ride and a Bredell Richardson Grab Win It
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane Green Wave (5-5) 20, Rice Owls (1-9) 17, Sat., Nov. 14, First Community Stadium, Houston. Next: vs North Texas, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans
articles.text:
Wave fans, what a weekend for this team. Tulane 20, Rice 17 on Saturday night at First Community Stadium in Houston, and we're 5-5. Friday's nationwide air traffic ground stop forced a change of plans, so the team rode a bus and rolled into Houston around 2 a.m. Saturday. Then they went out and won a football game. I'm so proud I could burst.

It wasn't pretty for a while. Rice led 17-6 at halftime after Jamir Benjamin intercepted Trace Johnson and ran it back 62 yards with 31 seconds left in the half. I sat in the stands thinking about that bus ride and wondering how much these guys had left.

Turns out they had plenty. DJ Dugar punched it in from 1 yard late in the third quarter to make it 17-13. Early in the fourth, J. Moore knocked the ball loose from Tyvonn Byars, and Dickson Agu recovered at the Rice 34. Three plays later, Johnson lofted one to the left pylon, and Bredell Richardson pulled it down for a 24-yard touchdown. 20-17 with about 10 minutes left. I screamed so loud the people around me turned and stared.

Then the defense had to hold, with a stiff crosswind blowing. Rice ground out a drive of more than seven minutes to our 20, and on fourth-and-1, Makai Williams stopped Gael Ochoa for no gain. Williams finished with 12 tackles. Agu had 10 and a fumble recovery. Anthony Rogers made two tackles for loss, and Jah'rie Garner had a sack. Rice got the ball back once more and never reached midfield.

Maurice Turner ran for 90 yards, including a 45-yard burst. Cooper Helmke made field goals from 35 and 41 yards. We converted 3 of 4 on fourth down too.

Five and five, with a long night's sleep coming. These guys earned it.

Roll Wave! The Tulane Green Wave host North Texas at Yulman Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Mississippi State vs Auburn: Four Fumbles and a Long Night in Starkville
articles.byline: Wade Pettus, The Mississippi State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Auburn Tigers (6-4) 41, Mississippi State Bulldogs (4-6) 9, Sat., Nov. 14, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville. Next: vs Tennessee Tech, Sat., Nov. 21, 1:00 PM ET, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville
articles.text:
Bulldog fans, I stayed until the end, because that's what we do. Auburn 41, Mississippi State 9. That was Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium. It leaves us at 4-6. We lost four fumbles, and you can't give a team like Auburn that many presents and expect a different result.

It felt competitive for a little while. AJ Swann found Sanfrisco Magee for a 34-yard touchdown nine seconds into the second quarter, and it was 10-7. Auburn then missed a long field goal, and we had the ball and some momentum. Then the football started hitting the turf. Swann was strip-sacked, and the return set Auburn up at our 1. Parker Puckett was sacked and lost it too. Kolin Wilson fumbled near midfield. By halftime it was 27-7, and the air had gone out of the place.

There were still people playing hard. Zakari Tillman made 10 tackles and broke up a throw. AJ Rice had nine stops, and Kendel Dolby had eight. Fatt Forrest intercepted a throw in the first quarter. Anthony Evans III caught four balls for 89 yards. Fluff Bothwell ran for 36. Those guys didn't quit.

The offense never found a rhythm after that early score. We ran 46 times for 46 yards. We went 3 of 16 on third down and came up short on fourth down three times, including at the Auburn 2 early in the fourth quarter. The next play was a safety. Kyle Ferrie also missed a 33-yard field goal in the first quarter. That's a lot of missed chances in one afternoon.

Four and six at home in November is a tough sit. But this program has been through worse, and I'm not walking away from it.

Come support these seniors. Go Dawgs. The Mississippi State Bulldogs host Tennessee Tech at Davis Wade Stadium, Nov. 21, 1 PM ET.

articles.title: Auburn vs Mississippi State: Four Recovered Fumbles, Six Wins, and a Loud Road Trip
articles.matchup: Final: Auburn Tigers (6-4) 41, Mississippi State Bulldogs (4-6) 9, Sat., Nov. 14, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville. Next: vs Samford, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn
articles.text:
Tiger fans, I made the drive to Starkville, and I am still hoarse. Auburn 41, Mississippi State 9 on Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium, and we're 6-4. That's six wins, and we can go to a bowl for the first time since 2023. I didn't care that it was a road game. I sang War Eagle anyway.

The defense set the table all afternoon. We recovered four fumbles, and those takeaways led to 24 points. Midway through the second quarter, Shadarius Toodle strip-sacked AJ Swann, Darrion Smith scooped it and ran to the 1, and Byrum Brown walked it in on the next snap. Nate Johnson then sacked Parker Puckett and forced another fumble that J. Smith recovered. R. Pleasant fell on one more. When we hit the quarterback, everything else opened up.

Brown completed 19 of 26 throws for 232 yards and three touchdowns. He found Keshaun Singleton for 26 yards in the first quarter and 42 yards in the third, and he hit Chas Nimrod for 35 yards in between. Singleton finished with seven catches for 103 yards. Jeremiah Cobb ran 10 yards for a score, and Alex McPherson made field goals of 37 and 31 yards. We had 371 yards and never trailed.

Mississippi State got a 34-yard touchdown throw to Sanfrisco Magee early in the second quarter and a safety in the fourth when we were tackled in our own end zone. That was it. Toodle finished with 10 tackles, a sack and two for loss. Da'Shawn Womack and Eric Winters each made eight stops.

Coach Alex Golesh said six wins means we get to keep practicing, and he also said the standard at Auburn is competing for championships. I agree with both. This was a big step. It is not the last one.

I'll be in my orange, yelling. War Eagle! The Auburn Tigers host Samford at Jordan-Hare Stadium, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Fresno State vs Texas State: A 35-31 Lead Slips Away in San Marcos
articles.byline: Rosalind 'Roz' Ayala, The Fresno State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas State Bobcats (6-4) 37, Fresno State Bulldogs (5-5) 35, Sat., Nov. 14, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos. Next: vs Colorado State, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno
articles.text:
Bulldog fans, I flew to San Marcos believing we were going to steal this one. For a long stretch in the fourth quarter, we had. Texas State 37, Fresno State 35 on Saturday at UFCU Stadium, and we're 5-5. We led 35-31 with 10:33 left, and we couldn't finish it.

The afternoon started with a jolt. After Texas State scored first, Rayshon Luke took the kickoff 100 yards to the house, and it was 7-7 just like that. I was still standing when he reached the end zone. Jayden Mandal then found Brock Lium for a 2-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and Bryson Donelson punched in scores from 1 yard and, later, from 2 yards to give us that 35-31 lead. Ryan Kobzeff's 19-yard run late in the third got us within 31-28. Mandal finished 20 of 34 for 250 yards.

Josiah Freeman caught six balls for 69 yards. The defense, led by Gerayas Grimes and his 14 tackles, hung in there too. Croix Stewart forced a fumble at our goal in the fourth quarter, and Grimes recovered it in the end zone for a touchback. K'vion Thunderbird had a sack. For a minute, it felt like we had this game in our hands.

Then it got away. Michael Patterson intercepted Mandal with 3:39 left, and Texas State drove 53 yards and scored with a minute to go. We got the ball back, but Mandal lost the football on a scramble, and Texas State recovered at our 4 with 48 seconds left. That was the end of it. We also missed a 51-yard field goal in the first quarter. Those are the snaps you want back.

Five and five. This one is going to sit with me all week.

Come home, Dogs. Let's answer this. The Fresno State Bulldogs host Colorado State at Valley Children's Stadium, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.
