articles.title: Texas State vs Fresno State: Davian Jackson Wins It With a Minute Left
articles.byline: Yesenia Calderwood, The Texas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas State Bobcats (6-4) 37, Fresno State Bulldogs (5-5) 35, Sat., Nov. 14, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos. Next: vs Washington State, Sat., Nov. 21, 6:00 PM ET, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos
articles.text:
Bobcat fans, my heart is still in my throat. Texas State 37, Fresno State 35 on Saturday at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, and we're 6-4. We led, we trailed, and then Davian Jackson punched it in from 2 yards with a minute left. I hugged the stranger next to me, and neither of us apologized.

Brad Jackson was brilliant. He completed 25 of 33 throws for 355 yards and three touchdowns. Zechariah Sample caught scoring throws of 12 and 30 yards in the first quarter. Chris Dawn Jr. took a 59-yarder to the house in the second. Beau Sparks had nine catches for 115 yards, and Sample finished with 95 yards on five grabs. Dawn had 99 on five. When those three are open, this offense is a joy.

Torrance Burgess Jr. ran 21 times for 107 yards and kept the chains moving. Davian Jackson also scored from 4 yards in the first quarter. We finished with 550 yards and 195 on the ground. Jacob Bonilla added a 35-yard field goal in the third quarter.

It got tight, though. After we led 31-21, Fresno State ran one in from 19 yards, then another from 2, and suddenly we were down 35-31 with 10:33 left. Burgess fumbled at the goal later, and they got the ball back. Michael Patterson III then intercepted a throw near midfield, and that gave us the chance we needed. Nine plays, 53 yards, and Jackson found the end zone. The extra point was blocked, so it stayed 37-35, and then J. Landry recovered a fumble at their 4 with 48 seconds left to close it.

Four wins in our last five. This building was loud, and I was louder.

I'll be here early. Go Cats! The Texas State Bobcats host Washington State at UFCU Stadium, Nov. 21, 6 PM ET.

articles.title: Boston College vs Notre Dame: A Long Day in South Bend
articles.byline: Siobhan Dunleavy, The Boston College Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) 41, Boston College Eagles (4-6) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame. Next: vs Syracuse, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA), Chestnut Hill
articles.text:
Eagle fans, I made the trip to Notre Dame Stadium, and I sat through every snap. Notre Dame 41, Boston College 7. That was Saturday. It leaves us at 4-6. They led 31-0 at halftime, and for most of the afternoon we couldn't get out of our own way. That's a hard thing to write, and it's a harder thing to watch.

We finished with 136 yards, including 51 through the air. Mason McKenzie completed 8 of 21 throws. We went 2 of 14 on third down and came up short on fourth down four times. Those numbers tell the story better than I can.

There was a spark in the third quarter. KP Price intercepted a throw at the Notre Dame 27, and a few plays later Bo MacCormack III ran it in from 3 yards. Price also had a sack. Anthony Palano led us with 11 tackles. Kemori Dixon and Marcus Upton each made eight, and Charlie Comella had seven. Those guys kept running to the ball long after the score got ugly.

MacCormack added 29 rushing yards, and Mekhi Dodd ran for 45, including a 19-yard burst. We just never sustained anything. A fumble in the second quarter was returned for a Notre Dame touchdown, and we threw an interception later. When you give a team like this extra possessions, they cash them in.

I still believe in this group. Four and six isn't where we wanted to be, but this season isn't finished, and neither are these seniors. We have two more Saturdays to show who we are, and I want to see this team play loose, play fast and have some fun doing it.

A home Saturday, a chance to feel like ourselves again. Go Eagles. The Boston College Eagles host Syracuse at Alumni Stadium, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.text:
Irish fans, that is exactly how you answer a week of questions. Notre Dame 41, Boston College 7 on Saturday at Notre Dame Stadium, and we're 9-1. Last Saturday we beat Miami. This Saturday we led 31-0 at halftime. The student section never sat down, and neither did I.

CJ Carr was in command. He completed 20 of 28 throws for 217 yards and two touchdowns, finding Micah Gilbert for 26 yards in the first quarter and Jordan Faison for 13 in the third. Jonaz Walton ran 15 times for 141 yards and punched in a 1-yard score. Nolan James Jr. added 73 yards and a 10-yard touchdown. We ran for 276 yards and finished with 500 yards of offense. That's the product I want to see every week.

The second quarter was a demolition. James scored, Walton scored, and then Jaylen Sneed returned a fumble 1 yard for another touchdown. Spencer Porath drilled a 40-yard field goal as the half expired, then added a 37-yarder in the fourth. Five extra points, two field goals, no misses. I love that kid.

Boston College got on the board after KP Price intercepted Carr early in the third quarter, and Bo MacCormack III ran it in from 3 yards. Fair enough. We answered right away with Faison's touchdown, and the rest of the afternoon was ours. Ethan Long picked off a throw later, and the Eagles came up empty on fourth down four times.

Coach Marcus Freeman said the leadership was spot on this week, and the guys understood the challenge in front of them. There was a lot of talk about 1993, when a big win was followed by a home loss to Boston College. This team blocked that out and played its game.

Nine and one. The gold helmets still shine.

I'll be in my seat early. Go Irish! The Notre Dame Fighting Irish host SMU at Notre Dame Stadium, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Michigan vs Oregon: Savion Hiter's 70-Yard Run Is the Lone Bright Spot
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon Ducks (7-3) 31, Michigan Wolverines (5-5) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Autzen Stadium, Eugene. Next: vs UCLA, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor
articles.text:
Wolverines, I flew out to Eugene hoping for a turnaround. I got a long flight home. Oregon 31, Michigan 7 on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, and we're 5-5. One more win gets us bowl eligible in Kyle Whittingham's first season, and right now that's what I'm holding onto.

The week was rough before we even got on the plane. After last week's 15-6 loss to Michigan State, the offensive coordinator was let go. Then on Saturday, Oregon hit a 60-yard touchdown on its opening drive, and we were chasing all day.

There was one moment I'll keep. Early in the second quarter, down 14-0, Savion Hiter took a handoff and went 70 yards for a touchdown. I was the only one standing in my row, and I didn't care. Hiter finished with 107 yards on 13 carries. Bryson Kuzdzal ran for 46 and Tommy Carr for 43. We ran for 215 yards. That part of the plan worked.

The rest didn't. We completed 6 of 20 throws for 71 yards between Carr and Bryce Underwood. We went 0 for 3 on fourth down and lost two fumbles in the fourth quarter. Oregon threw for 341 yards, and a 59-yard touchdown with six seconds left in the first half made it 21-7. That one hurt.

Chris Bracy had a sack and eight tackles. Zeke Berry made eight stops, and Troy Bowles had seven. J. Hill broke up a fourth-down throw in the second quarter. The defense kept swinging even when the offense couldn't help.

This is a hard season. It's not the Michigan I grew up with. But the Big House is still the Big House, and Saturday is a chance to send this team into a bowl.

Go Blue. The Michigan Wolverines host UCLA at Michigan Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Oregon vs Michigan: Dylan Raiola Throws Four Touchdowns at a Rocking Autzen
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon Ducks (7-3) 31, Michigan Wolverines (5-5) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Autzen Stadium, Eugene. Next: at Michigan State, Fri., Nov. 20, 8:00 PM ET, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing
articles.text:
Ducks, it never gets old. Oregon 31, Michigan 7 on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, and we're 7-3 with three straight wins. Shout went full volume in the fourth quarter, and I was jumping so hard my bucket hat flew two rows down.

Dylan Raiola was lights out. Twenty of 28 for 341 yards and four touchdowns. On our opening drive, he found Jeremiah McClellan for a 60-yard touchdown. He hit Da'Jaun Riggs for a 2-yarder late in the first quarter. Then with six seconds left before halftime, he dropped one in to Dakorien Moore for 59 yards and a 21-7 lead. That throw had Autzen shaking. In the fourth quarter, he found Dierre Hill Jr. for 49 more.

McClellan caught four balls for 105 yards. Moore had seven for 101. Hill ran 21 times for 98 yards and caught that touchdown. Gage Hurych finished it with a 21-yard field goal in the final minute.

And the defense smothered the Wolverines. Michigan threw for 71 yards, completing 6 of 20 throws. They came up short on fourth down three times. Matayo Uiagalelei had two sacks and kept their quarterbacks running for their lives. Dylan Williams made 11 tackles and forced a fumble. B. Alexander forced another, and B. Finney and N. Offord fell on them. We gave up a 70-yard run early in the second quarter, and that was the only time Michigan found the end zone.

Raiola said the team is aware of what could happen but focused on handling its own business. That's the right attitude. We need some help to reach the Playoff, but you can't get help if you don't win, and this team keeps winning.

Short week, Ducks. Let's keep it rolling. Go Ducks! The Oregon Ducks travel to face Michigan State in East Lansing, Friday, Nov. 20, 8 PM ET.

articles.title: Jacksonville State vs Western Kentucky: A Lead Slips Away in the Final Seconds
articles.byline: Burl Ashcraft-Neeley, The Jacksonville State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (4-6) 34, Jacksonville State Gamecocks (7-3) 24, Sat., Nov. 14, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green. Next: vs Missouri State, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville
articles.text:
Gamecock fans, I don't know if I've ever felt this sick after a football game. Western Kentucky 34, Jacksonville State 24. That was Saturday in Bowling Green. It leaves us at 7-3. We led 24-21 from late in the second quarter until two seconds were left. Two seconds.

The first half was a blast. Garrison Rippa drilled a 50-yard field goal. Eleven seconds later, Jacob Cruz scooped up a fumble and ran it 8 yards for a touchdown. Caleb Nix intercepted a throw. Caden Creel threw touchdowns to Jamill Williams from 9 yards and Luke Gilbert from 7. 24-21 at halftime, and I was feeling great.

Then the offense went quiet. We didn't score in the second half. We came up short on fourth down three times, including on a deep throw in the third quarter and at their 9 a little later. Creel fumbled at our 25 too. We ran for 48 yards all day, and that put everything on Creel's shoulders. He went 17 of 25 for 164 yards and two scores. Deondre Johnson had a 63-yard catch.

The defense did its part for a long time. Nix had nine tackles to go with the interception. Myles Butler made eight. Cruz recovered another fumble in the third quarter to stop a WKU drive. They kept Western Kentucky out of the end zone the whole second half, until the very end.

With 4:44 left, we punted, and WKU drove 58 yards and scored with two seconds left. Then on the kickoff, the ball came loose and they recovered it in the end zone. Ten points in two seconds. The scoreboard says 34-24, but it was a lot closer than that.

I hate this one. But 7-3 is still a good season, and this team will be fine.

Let's come home and get back to winning, Gamecocks. The Jacksonville State Gamecocks host Missouri State at AmFirst Stadium, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: Western Kentucky vs Jacksonville State: Brock Glenn Wins It With Two Seconds Left
articles.byline: Thurman 'Tops' Whitsitt, The Western Kentucky Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (4-6) 34, Jacksonville State Gamecocks (7-3) 24, Sat., Nov. 14, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green. Next: at Liberty, Sat., Nov. 21, 1:00 PM ET, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg
articles.text:
Hilltopper Nation, I'm still shaking. Western Kentucky 34, Jacksonville State 24 on Saturday at Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium in Bowling Green, and we're 4-6. We trailed for almost the entire second half, and we won it with two seconds on the clock. Red towels everywhere. Mine is soaked.

Let's go to the finish first, because I've already watched it again more times than I can count. Down 24-21, we got the ball at our 42 with 4:44 left. Brock Glenn led an 11-play, 58-yard drive, picked up a key first down with his legs, and then, with two seconds left, he hit Jyziah Rockwell for a 10-yard touchdown. The Hill exploded. Then on the final kickoff, Jacksonville State tried a few laterals, the ball hit the turf and Dave Herard fell on it in the end zone. Final whistle, and I hugged everybody around me.

Glenn was the story. He ran for two touchdowns in the first half, from 4 and 1 yards, and finished with 71 rushing yards. Ajay Allen ran in a 6-yarder in the first quarter. Rodney Tisdale Jr. went 14 of 16, and Glenn went 7 of 10 with the winning throw. Zion Taylor caught six balls.

And the defense kept us alive through a scoreless second half. Jaylen Lewis picked off a throw right before halftime and then broke up a deep fourth-down throw in the third quarter. Jaylen Wester forced a fumble and recovered it himself. Late in the third, we stuffed them on fourth down at our 9. Jacksonville State had 212 yards and 48 on the ground. Westen Ard made eight tackles, and Justin Brown had two for loss.

We held the ball for more than 37 minutes. It just took us until the last snap to make it count.

Bring that magic with you, Tops. The Western Kentucky Hilltoppers travel to face Liberty in Lynchburg, Nov. 21, 1 PM ET.

articles.title: Northern Illinois vs Nevada: A Long Afternoon in DeKalb, but DeAree Rogers Keeps Fighting
articles.byline: Nola Brandvik, The Northern Illinois Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Nevada Wolf Pack (4-6) 28, Northern Illinois Huskies (0-10) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Huskie Stadium, Dekalb. Next: at North Dakota State, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, Fargodome, Fargo
articles.text:
Huskie fans, no sugarcoating tonight. Nevada 28, Northern Illinois 7. That was Saturday at Huskie Stadium. It leaves us at 0-10. The scoreboard wasn't kind, and the stands weren't full. But I was there, and I'll be there next week too, because that's what you do for your team.

It went sideways early. Our very first drive ended in an interception, and in the second quarter, a fumble at midfield gave Nevada the ball right back. By halftime it was 21-0. Nevada ran the ball 51 times for 308 yards, and our defense spent a lot of the afternoon chasing.

There were bright spots, and I want to point them out. Brady Kerperin and Jack Murray each made 11 tackles. Liam Lindo intercepted a throw in our end zone late in the fourth quarter. Andruw Ellis made seven stops. Those guys kept playing hard right to the final whistle, and our seniors deserve a lot of credit for the way they keep showing up every single week.

Taron Dickens threw for 194 yards. DeAree Rogers was a warrior with 10 catches for 64 yards, and with 4:16 left, he caught a 5-yard touchdown from Dickens to get us on the board. La'Don Bryant had a 35-yard catch. Our offense moved the ball some, but we ran for 68 yards and committed 10 penalties for 107 yards. You can't play from behind like that. Nevada also stopped us on fourth down twice in the fourth quarter.

Zero wins is hard. It's hard on the players, it's hard on the coaches and it's hard on those of us who drive in from Sycamore and Rochelle and everywhere else to watch. But this program has a proud history, and nobody here is quitting.

One win. That's all I want this season. One.

Big challenge, big chance. Go Huskies. The Northern Illinois Huskies travel to face North Dakota State in Fargo, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET.

articles.title: Nevada vs Northern Illinois: Herschel Turner Runs for 153 and the Pack Rolls in DeKalb
articles.matchup: Final: Nevada Wolf Pack (4-6) 28, Northern Illinois Huskies (0-10) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Huskie Stadium, Dekalb. Next: vs Hawai'i, Sat., Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET, Mackay Stadium, Reno
articles.text:
Wolf Pack, that's how you take a road trip. Nevada 28, Northern Illinois 7 on Saturday at Huskie Stadium in DeKalb, and we're 4-6. I traded the Sierra for the cornfields for a weekend, and the boys made it worth every mile.

Herschel Turner was a man on a mission. Thirteen carries, 153 yards, almost 12 yards every time he touched it. He opened the scoring with a 6-yard run in the first quarter and then broke a 29-yarder early in the second. We ran for 308 yards as a team, and AJ Bianco added 90 of them on 13 carries. When the ground game works like that, everything works.

And Trace Estes? Two catches. Two touchdowns. A 51-yarder from Bianco in the second quarter that made it 21-0, and a 22-yarder in the third that made it 28-0. Efficiency, my friends. Bianco only needed 13 throws all afternoon.

The defense had Northern Illinois in a headlock. Joshua Scott picked off a throw on the Huskies' very first drive. E. Smith forced a fumble early in the second quarter that I. Jordan recovered. David Paine Jr. was a terror with two sacks. Jeremy Naborne-Owens had a tackle and a half for loss and broke up a throw, and Aiden Walker made seven tackles. NIU ran for 68 yards and didn't score until 4:16 left. Brandon Amaniampong recovered a fumble in the final minute to finish it off.

We did leave some points out there. We came up short on fourth down twice and threw an interception in the end zone late. But a 21-0 halftime lead on the road is something I'll gladly take.

This team keeps getting better, and Reno should be excited about what's coming next.

Let's pack Mackay and keep this rolling. Go Pack! The Nevada Wolf Pack host Hawai'i at Mackay Stadium, Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Middle Tennessee vs Liberty: Blue Raiders Push the Unbeaten Flames to the Wire
articles.byline: Opal Stonebriar, The Middle Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty Flames (9-1) 28, Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders (5-5) 23, Sat., Nov. 14, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg. Next: at Sam Houston, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville
articles.text:
Blue Raider fans, I'm frustrated, I'm proud and I'm hoarse. Liberty 28, Middle Tennessee 23. That was Saturday at Williams Stadium in Lynchburg. It leaves us at 5-5. Liberty came in unbeaten in the league and just clinched a spot in the title game, and we had them sweating with six minutes left.

Roman Gagliano was terrific. Twenty-four of 34 for 202 yards and two touchdowns, plus 47 yards on the ground. Cam'ron Lacy caught 10 balls for 97 yards and was open every time I looked up. Ziyon Butler made a 23-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter that cut it to 21-17. And Neo Clifton, my goodness, Neo Clifton. With 6:18 left, he reached out one hand around a defender and snagged a 14-yard touchdown. That catch belongs on a poster in Murfreesboro.

Dominic Bourgeois hit a 45-yard field goal, and Antonio Martin punched in an 8-yard run in the second quarter to give us a 10-7 lead. We were right in it the whole way.

The defense made some big plays. Korey Smith was everywhere, with 16 tackles. Reggie Johnson sacked the quarterback in the first quarter and knocked the ball loose, and Ashton Taylor recovered it. We stopped Liberty on fourth down twice and turned both of those stops into touchdowns.

But Liberty ran for 370 yards. You can't give up that much on the ground and win on the road. And after Clifton's catch, the two-point try failed and we never got the ball back with a real chance. Liberty held it for more than 36 minutes, and that was the game.

We're 5-5. One more and we're bowl eligible. That's in front of us, and this team plays hard every week.

Let's go get number six, Blue Raiders. The Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders travel to face Sam Houston in Huntsville, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: Liberty vs Middle Tennessee: Nine Straight and a Ticket to the CUSA Title Game
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty Flames (9-1) 28, Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders (5-5) 23, Sat., Nov. 14, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg. Next: vs Western Kentucky, Sat., Nov. 21, 1:00 PM ET, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg
articles.text:
Flames Nation, book the trip! Liberty 28, Middle Tennessee 23 on Saturday at Williams Stadium in Lynchburg, and we're 9-1, 6-0 in Conference USA and headed to the championship game on Dec. 4. Nine straight wins. Praise the Lord, and somebody save me a slice of pie.

We ran the ball 53 times for 370 yards. Three hundred seventy! Kam Davis carried it 20 times for 126 yards, including a 23-yard touchdown early in the third quarter that made it 21-10. Jaylon Coleman broke a 45-yarder for our first score, and he only needed seven carries to get 84 yards. Terron Kellman and Deshawn Purdie each chipped in more than 40. Jaylin Belford punched in a 3-yarder right before halftime.

Purdie didn't need to throw much, but when he did, he made it count. Early in the fourth quarter, he hit Makai Jackson for a 10-yard touchdown that made it 28-17. Jackson caught five balls for 50 yards.

Now, I'll be honest, this one got tighter than I liked. We came up short on fourth down twice in our own territory, and Middle Tennessee scored both times. Then they hit a one-handed touchdown catch with 6:18 left that had me clutching my seat cushion. But their two-point try failed, and we held the ball and the lead the rest of the way. We had the ball for more than 36 minutes.

Brenton Williams had a sack, Dillano Glaud broke up a throw, and Ronald Moore Jr. made a tackle for loss. Middle Tennessee ran for 88 yards, and that's what kept us in front.

Jamey Chadwell's teams know how to win in November. Now we get to see if we can win in December.

Fill the place, Lynchburg. Go Flames! The Liberty Flames host Western Kentucky at Williams Stadium, Nov. 21, 1 PM ET.

articles.title: Georgia State vs Georgia Southern: Hot Start, Cold Finish in a 34-17 Loss
articles.byline: Malik Overstreet, The Georgia State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern Eagles (6-4) 34, Georgia State Panthers (5-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 14, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at Marshall, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington
articles.text:
Panther fans, that first quarter was everything I wanted from a rivalry game in downtown Atlanta. The rest of it? Not so much. Georgia Southern 34, Georgia State 17 on Saturday at Center Parc Stadium, and we're 5-5.

We came out swinging. Qwantavius Wiggins plowed in from 3 yards midway through the first quarter. Then D. Lee scooped up a Max Johnson fumble at their 10, and Lanear McCrary Jr. scored from 7 yards out with 38 seconds left in the quarter. 14-7, Panthers. The student section was going nuts, and I was screaming right along with them.

McCrary was our best weapon all day, 13 carries for 86 yards, including a 49-yard run. We ran for 146 yards as a team and held the ball for almost 33 minutes. That's how we wanted to play.

But the second quarter flipped everything. They tied it 15 seconds in on a 52-yard throw, kicked a field goal, and scored again with 25 seconds before the half. We went into the locker room down 24-14, and we never found the end zone again.

Tyson McCrary picked off a throw in the third quarter and made nine tackles. Donovan Faria had nine stops of his own. Samer Layous hit a 37-yarder in the third to make it 24-17. And then the fourth quarter got away from us: a missed 34-yarder, a blocked 43-yarder and a 54-yard touchdown run by their backup quarterback.

Ayden Pereira went 14 of 19, but for only 75 yards. We have to stretch the field somehow. Teams are going to keep loading up on the run until we do.

We're 5-5, and a bowl is still right there. This team has the fight to get it.

One win from six. Let's go, Panthers. The Georgia State Panthers travel to face Marshall in Huntington, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET.

articles.title: Georgia Southern vs Georgia State: Eagles Shut the Door and Grab First in the East
articles.byline: Royce Ogeechee, The Georgia Southern Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern Eagles (6-4) 34, Georgia State Panthers (5-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 14, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at Troy, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL), Troy
articles.text:
Hail Southern! Georgia Southern 34, Georgia State 17 on Saturday at Center Parc Stadium in Atlanta, and we're 6-4 and 5-1 in the Sun Belt with a half-game lead atop the East. Four straight wins. Five of the last six. Statesboro, get loud.

It was a fight early. Georgia State scored twice on short runs in the first quarter, and we trailed 14-7. Then Max Johnson owned the second quarter. Fifteen seconds in, he hit River Helms for a 52-yard touchdown to tie it 14-14. Tripp Bryant kicked a 42-yarder, and with 25 seconds before the half, Johnson found Josh Dallas from 13 yards out. 24-14, Eagles. I hugged my cousin from Brooklet and spilled boiled peanuts all over both of us.

Johnson finished 16 of 22 for 203 yards and two touchdowns. Alex Taylor caught six balls for 92 yards, including a 41-yarder, and Helms had four for 75. Taeo Todd ran for 77 and David Mbadinga added 63. Then Weston Bryan, who'd already thrown for 41, broke a 54-yard touchdown run with 4:11 left to put it away.

But the defense is why we're in first place. Georgia State never sniffed the end zone in the second half. The Panthers threw for 75 yards all game. Brandon Tyson was a heat-seeking missile with 14 tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss, and he made the final stop on fourth down in the last minute. Jakyri Jones and Eli Anders each had a sack, and our special teams blocked a 43-yard field goal in the fourth.

We did put the ball on the ground twice and threw an interception, so the coaches will have a few things to say on Monday. But a road win in Atlanta, a division lead and a defense playing like this? I'll take it every week.

Keep it rolling, Eagles. Hail Southern! The Georgia Southern Eagles travel to face Troy in Troy, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET.

articles.title: Cal vs Virginia: Golden Bears Give Away Two Touchdowns in a 36-7 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Virginia Cavaliers (5-5) 36, California Golden Bears (3-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville. Next: vs Stanford, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley
articles.text:
Golden Bears, it was a long way to fly for that. Virginia 36, California 7. That was Saturday at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville. It leaves us at 3-7. That's four straight losses. I'm writing this from a hotel lobby with a cup of tea that's gone cold, and that feels about right.

The game turned on one play near halftime. We were down 9-0 and driving with 2:11 left, and we tried a trick play, a throw from M. Mini. Virginia picked it off in its own end zone and ran it back 100 yards. Instead of a two-point game, it was 16-0. I put my head in my hands, and I left it there for a while.

We did answer. Adam Mohammed punched in a 5-yard touchdown with 14 seconds left in the half, and it was 16-7 at the break. Mohammed ran hard all day, and Mark Hamper caught six balls for 66 yards.

But the second half didn't go our way. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele threw two interceptions, and the second one came back 33 yards for a Virginia touchdown with four seconds left in the third quarter. That made it 26-7. We ran for 42 yards and had 201 for the game. It's hard to win when you can't get anything going on the ground.

The defense hung in longer than the final score says. AJ Tuitele made 11 tackles. Kingston Lopa had eight. Cam Sidney broke up a throw. Virginia went 7 of 16 on third down, and we kept a couple of drives to field goals. When your offense gives up 14 points on its own, though, the defense can only do so much.

I'm not giving up on these kids. Justin Wilcox's teams always fight, and the biggest game of the year is next.

It's Big Game week. Forget the record. Beat Stanford. Go Bears! The California Golden Bears host Stanford at California Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Virginia vs Cal: Two Interception Returns and a Skid Snapped at Scott Stadium
articles.matchup: Final: Virginia Cavaliers (5-5) 36, California Golden Bears (3-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville. Next: vs North Carolina, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:30 PM ET, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville
articles.text:
Wahoos, the sky is not falling. Virginia 36, California 7 on Saturday at Scott Stadium, and the three-game losing streak is history. We're 5-5 and 5-1 at home. After that 51-7 loss at Wake Forest on Oct. 31, Tony Elliott told the team to dig its feet in. They dug.

The defense scored twice, and both were jaw-droppers. With 2:00 left in the first half, Cal tried a little trickery, and Brandyn Hillman picked it off in our end zone and ran 100 yards the other way. One hundred! I spilled my hot cider on a perfectly nice gentleman from Albemarle County, and he didn't even mind. Then, with four seconds left in the third quarter, Kam Robinson jumped a throw at the Cal 33 and took it to the house.

Robinson was the best player on the field. Twelve tackles plus that touchdown. Montino Williams picked off a third throw in the fourth quarter after Myles Brown tipped it. We sacked their quarterback four times and held the Golden Bears to 201 yards and 42 on the ground.

Beau Pribula ran the offense well, 16 of 24 for 146 yards, with a 12-yard touchdown to Da'Shawn Martin in the first quarter and a 43-yard run. Eli Holstein came in and hit a few throws, including a 35-yarder to Jack Rhodes. Solomon Beebe ran six times for 58 yards. Will Bettridge was perfect on field goals from 30, 30 and 42. Xay Davis punched in the last touchdown.

We went 3 for 3 on fourth down and held the ball for nearly 35 minutes. That's how you get back on your feet.

Mr. Jefferson would be proud. Well, maybe not of the penalties.

The South's Oldest Rivalry, with a bowl at stake. Wahoowa! The Virginia Cavaliers host North Carolina at Scott Stadium, Nov. 21, 12:30 PM ET.

articles.title: West Virginia vs Kansas: A 30-7 Halftime Hole Sinks the Mountaineers
articles.byline: Jolene Buckhannon, The West Virginia Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kansas Jayhawks (4-6) 37, West Virginia Mountaineers (5-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown. Next: vs Houston, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown
articles.text:
Mountaineers, I'm going to sit on my porch tonight and listen to the hills, because I don't want to talk to anybody. Kansas 37, West Virginia 14. That was Saturday at Milan Puskar Stadium. It leaves us at 5-5. That was a long, cold afternoon in Morgantown.

It went wrong right away. On our second snap of the game, a throw got picked off by a former Mountaineer, of all people. Kansas kicked a field goal, scored again on the next drive, and it was 10-0 before we had our coats buttoned. Michael Hawkins Jr. answered with a 2-yard touchdown run to make it 10-7, and for about four minutes the stadium believed. Then Kansas scored 20 straight to close the half, and it was 30-7 at the break, the worst halftime spot we've been in all year.

We couldn't stop their quarterback. He ran for 164 yards and completed 15 of 18 throws, and Kansas ran for 296 as a team. They held the ball for nearly 37 minutes. Our defense was on the field so long I started to feel sorry for them.

Some guys never stopped. Cam Torbor made 11 tackles. Isaiah Patterson and ChaMarryus Bomar each had nine, and Patterson got a sack. Bomar intercepted a throw at our 2 in the second quarter to keep it from getting worse. Geimere Latimer II had two tackles for loss.

Hawkins battled, too. He threw for 227 yards and found John Neider for a 17-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. DJ Epps caught five balls for 51 yards, and TaRon Francis had a 38-yarder. But 35 rushing yards won't win you anything in this league.

We're 5-5, and that means one more win gets us to a bowl. That's still in front of us, and I'm still singing Country Roads at the end of every game, win or lose.

Let's go, Mountaineers. The West Virginia Mountaineers host Houston at Milan Puskar Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Kansas vs West Virginia: Isaiah Marshall Runs Wild in Morgantown
articles.matchup: Final: Kansas Jayhawks (4-6) 37, West Virginia Mountaineers (5-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 14, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown. Next: vs BYU, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence
articles.text:
Rock Chalk, Jayhawk! Kansas 37, West Virginia 14 on Saturday at Milan Puskar Stadium in Morgantown, and we're 4-6 with a pulse. I sang the alma mater in the visitors' section so loud a Mountaineer fan offered me a cough drop.

Isaiah Marshall, ladies and gentlemen. The sophomore ran 19 times for a career-high 164 yards, including a 50-yard burst, and five of his runs went for 10 or more. He completed his first nine throws and finished 15 of 18 for 152 yards. He even shook off a first-half knock and kept going. He punched in a 2-yarder with 45 seconds left in the half that made it 30-7, the biggest halftime hole West Virginia has been in all year.

And the guy who got it all started? Trey Lathan, a former Mountaineer, picked off a throw on West Virginia's second snap of the game. Leroy Harris III got his hand on it first. Talk about a homecoming. We kicked a 24-yard field goal, then Khijohnn Cummings-Coleman scored from 5 and from 26, and we were rolling. Chase Belcher added two more touchdown runs, from 2 and 8 yards.

We ran for 296 yards as a team and held the ball for nearly 37 minutes. That's Kansas football I want framed on my wall.

The defense was terrific too. West Virginia ran for 35 yards. Corey Gordon made 11 tackles, 10 of them solo. Harris had a sack and two tackles for loss, and Blake Herold got another sack. Q. Davis stuffed a fourth-down run early in the fourth quarter, and J. Conde broke up the Mountaineers' last fourth-down try in the final minute.

We still have hope for a bowl. Faint, sure, but hope. And after a day like this, I'll ride that hope all the way home on I-70.

Wave the wheat, Lawrence. The Kansas Jayhawks host BYU at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Missouri vs Georgia: A 31-0 Hole Was Too Deep in Athens
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Bulldogs (9-1) 48, Missouri Tigers (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Sanford Stadium, Athens. Next: vs Kentucky, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Memorial Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Tiger fans, I'll make this quick, because I don't want to relive the first quarter more than once. Georgia 48, Missouri 21. That was Saturday at Sanford Stadium in Athens. It leaves us at 6-4. The Bulldogs scored on their first five possessions, and by the middle of the second quarter it was 31-0. We came in ranked. We left humbled.

Our very first snap was intercepted and returned to our 7. That's not how you want to start in front of 93,033 people. Georgia scored on the next play, and from there it was like trying to stop a freight train with a paper plate.

Austin Simmons deserves credit for not quitting. He went 17 of 25 for 175 yards and three touchdowns: a 15-yarder to Naeshaun Montgomery in the second quarter, an 11-yarder to Donovan Olugbode late in the third and a 2-yarder to Kenric Lanier II in the fourth. Olugbode caught four for 67. Cayden Lee had a 34-yard grab. Jamal Roberts ran 19 times for 62 yards.

Robert Woodyard Jr. made 10 tackles, Elijah Dotson had nine and Nicholas Rodriguez got a sack. Georgia gained 468 yards, so those guys were busy all afternoon.

The numbers that hurt: we went 2 of 11 on third down, and Georgia completed 20 of 26 throws. You can't win between the hedges like that.

Here's the thing, though. We're 6-4 and bowl eligible, and the next one is at home. Nobody in Columbia is packing it in. Eli Drinkwitz's teams always bounce back, and I've watched this group answer tough losses before.

Georgia is the No. 1 team in the country for a reason. They have NFL bodies everywhere, a crowd that never sits down and a quarterback who barely misses. We'll learn from it. A loss in Athens is not a season, and this season still has a lot of football left in it.

Faurot Field at night, black and gold everywhere. M-I-Z! The Missouri Tigers host Kentucky at Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Georgia vs Missouri: Five Straight Scores and a 48-21 Rout Between the Hedges
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Bulldogs (9-1) 48, Missouri Tigers (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Sanford Stadium, Athens. Next: at South Carolina, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Dawg Nation, we're back on top and we celebrated like it. Georgia 48, Missouri 21 on Saturday at Sanford Stadium, and we're 9-1. The last time we got to No. 1, we tripped on Auburn the very next week. This time, the Dawgs came out angry.

Five possessions, five scores. We got the ball first and Nate Frazier ran it in from 4 yards. Then Missouri's first snap got picked off by Raylen Wilson, who brought it back 30 yards to their 7, and Gunner Stockton ran it in from 8. Frazier scored again from 3, Peyton Woodring kicked a 41-yarder and Stockton hit Isiah Canion for a 12-yard touchdown. 31-0, and the second quarter wasn't even half done. I hugged the man next to me, then his wife, then a stranger in a red sweater.

Stockton was in complete control: 18 of 24 for 252 yards and a touchdown, plus that rushing score. Craig Dandridge caught six balls for 85 yards. Talyn Taylor had three for 63. Dwight Phillips Jr. ran seven times for 66. Frazier finished with three short touchdown runs, and Chauncey Bowens added a fourth-quarter score.

The defense set the tone, and Kirby will be happy with how it held up while it mattered. Justin Williams made 10 tackles. Rasean Dinkins and Chris Cole each had a tackle for loss. Missouri went 2 of 11 on third down and had 286 yards, a lot of it after the outcome was decided.

Woodring hit from 41 and 40 and made all six extra points. That man is automatic.

Kirby said this team will be measured by November and the months after. I'm already planning my trips.

Night game, road crowd. Bring it on. Go Dawgs! The Georgia Bulldogs travel to face South Carolina in Columbia, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: USC vs Indiana: Three Interceptions Cost the Trojans in Bloomington
articles.matchup: Final: Indiana Hoosiers (9-1) 27, USC Trojans (7-3) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington. Next: vs Maryland, Sat., Nov. 21, 6:15 PM ET, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles
articles.text:
Trojan Family, I flew to Indiana in November, which tells you how much I love this team. Indiana 27, USC 13. That was Saturday at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington. It leaves us at 7-3. The defending champs earned it. We helped a little, and that's what stings.

For three quarters, we went toe to toe. Caden Chittenden hit a 29-yard field goal in the first quarter. Then, with 21 seconds left in the half, Jayden Maiava found Zacharyus Williams for a 7-yard touchdown to tie it 10-10. Chittenden added a 25-yarder in the third, and it was 13-13. Fight On, right there.

Trent Mosley was outstanding: nine catches for 130 yards. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt grabbed a 51-yarder. Mark Bowman caught six. Maiava threw for 311 yards and moved the ball all day. We outgained a lot of teams this year, and we nearly matched the champs yard for yard.

But three interceptions will beat you anywhere, and they beat us here. The worst came with 6:40 left. We had marched 83 yards to second-and-goal at their 6, down 20-13, with a chance to tie it, and the throw got picked off at the 1. Another came at 2:36 and was returned to our 29. And then Indiana hit a 42-yard touchdown. That's the game.

The defense battled. Desman Stephens II made eight tackles, Deven Bryant intercepted a throw right before halftime, and Alex VanSumeren and Bryant each made six stops. Indiana converted 7 of 13 third downs, though, and we were 2 of 11. That's the other story.

I don't love losing in the Midwest. But this team is 7-3 and still dangerous, and the Coliseum gets one more home game coming up.

Sunshine, the band, the horse. Let's go, Trojans. Fight On! The USC Trojans host Maryland at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Nov. 21, 6:15 PM ET.

articles.title: Indiana vs USC: Grant Wilson's First Start and Three Interceptions Keep the Champs Rolling
articles.matchup: Final: Indiana Hoosiers (9-1) 27, USC Trojans (7-3) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington. Next: at Washington, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Husky Stadium, Seattle
articles.text:
Hoosiers, the defending national champions are 9-1. Indiana 27, USC 13 on Saturday at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington. I still pinch myself every time I type that first sentence, and I've typed it a lot this year.

This one belonged to Grant Wilson. Seven college seasons, from Fordham to Old Dominion to Bloomington, and on Saturday he made his first start in cream and crimson. He went 17 of 27 for 305 yards and two touchdowns. He hit Brock Schott for a 13-yard score on our opening drive, and then with 3:30 left he dropped a 42-yarder into Charlie Becker's hands that put it away. He called it a blessing to be here. Grant, we feel the same about you.

It was tied 13-13 late in the third quarter when Khobie Martin plowed in from a yard out, and Memorial Stadium shook. Martin ran for 82 yards on 12 carries, including a 37-yarder. Nick Marsh had a 65-yard catch, and Shazz Preston grabbed a 47-yarder. Big plays all afternoon.

Now the defense, because these guys won the game. Three interceptions. Preston Zachman got one in the second quarter. With 6:40 left, USC had second-and-goal at our 6 after an 83-yard drive, and Isaiah Jones picked one off at the 1 and held on even after it got knocked loose. Then Jamari Sharpe grabbed one with 2:36 left and brought it back 34 yards. Jacob Savage made 13 tackles. USC converted 2 of 11 third downs.

Nico Radicic kicked field goals from 21 and 24 yards. Every point added up.

Coach Cignetti said Grant left a few plays out there. That's Coach. He'd say that about a perfect game. I'll say it plainly: this team just keeps winning.

Pack a rain jacket, Hoosiers. The Indiana Hoosiers travel to face Washington in Seattle, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: FIU vs Delaware: JJ Kohl Throws for 313, Panthers Fall 24-16 in Newark
articles.byline: Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, The Florida International Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware Blue Hens (5-5) 24, Florida International Panthers (4-6) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Delaware Stadium, Newark. Next: at Kennesaw State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:00 PM ET, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw
articles.text:
Panthers, I packed a winter coat for Newark, Delaware, and I still froze. Delaware 24, Florida International 16. That was Saturday at Delaware Stadium. It leaves us at 4-6. We're still looking for our first road win, and this one was right there.

JJ Kohl kept us in it. He threw for 313 yards on 26 completions, and Maguire Anderson was a monster with nine catches for 122 yards. Devonte Lyons ran it in from 2 yards in the first quarter to tie it at 7, and Robert Czeremcha hit a 30-yard field goal early in the fourth to tie it again at 10. Every time Delaware went ahead, we came back.

Then, after the Hens went up 17-10, Kohl found Tyson Carter for an 8-yard touchdown with 5:42 left. 17-16. And then the extra point got blocked. I put my hands on my head and kept them there for a long time.

The second quarter is the part that's going to bother me. We drove deep and came up empty on fourth down at their 1. Then our defense forced a fumble, D. Holmes Jr. knocking the ball loose and J. Taylor recovering it near midfield, and on the last play before halftime, a throw got intercepted at the goal. Two great chances, zero points.

The defense did a lot right. Jai-Ayviauynn Celestine and DeAndre Boykins made eight tackles each, and Percy Courtney Jr. got some heat on the quarterback. We held the ball for more than 35 minutes and converted 3 of 5 fourth downs. But their quarterback completed 27 of 30 throws, and you just can't give a guy that many easy ones.

We had one last shot with less than two minutes left and came up short on fourth down at the Delaware 45.

That first road win is out there. Let's go get it, Panthers. The Florida International Panthers travel to face Kennesaw State in Kennesaw, Nov. 21, 3 PM ET.

articles.title: Delaware vs FIU: Nick Minicucci Goes 27 of 30 and the Hens Never Trail
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware Blue Hens (5-5) 24, Florida International Panthers (4-6) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Delaware Stadium, Newark. Next: at New Mexico State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:00 PM ET, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces
articles.text:
Hens, gather round. Delaware 24, Florida International 16 on Saturday at Delaware Stadium in Newark, and we're 5-5 and 4-1 at home. We never trailed. Not once. On a cold Newark afternoon, that's the best kind of football there is.

Nick Minicucci was nearly perfect. Twenty-seven of 30 for 230 yards and two touchdowns, and he added 69 rushing yards, including a 62-yard dash that had the whole place on its feet. He hit Elijah Sessoms for an 11-yard touchdown in the first quarter, Viron Ellison Jr. for a 7-yarder in the fourth, and then ran in the clincher himself from a yard out with 3:49 left. Sean Wilson and Donovan Lewis each caught eight balls. Nick just kept finding them.

But this was a defensive day, too. FIU threw for 313 yards, and we still kept them out of the end zone when it counted most. Jawarren Corbin picked off a throw on their very first drive. Right before halftime, Kevin Moore intercepted one at our goal and brought it out 46 yards. Dominick Brogna broke up a fourth-down throw at our 1 in the second quarter. Gavin Moul was everywhere with 13 tackles, and Blake Matthews kept the quarterback running for his life.

When FIU scored with 5:42 left to make it 17-16, we blocked the extra point. Then Minicucci went right back down the field for the touchdown, and on FIU's last drive the defense got the stop on fourth down with 1:51 to go. We picked up a first down, and that was that.

Tucker Smack hit a 22-yard field goal in the third. Every point mattered today.

One more win and this team is bowl eligible. Newark, can you feel it?

Long trip, big chance. Go Hens! The Delaware Blue Hens travel to face New Mexico State in Las Cruces, Nov. 21, 3 PM ET.

Nick Minicucci was nearly perfect. Twenty-seven of 30 for 230 yards and two touchdowns, and he added 69 rushing yards, including a 62-yard dash that had the whole place on its feet. He hit Elijah Sessoms for an 11-yard touchdown in the first quarter, Viron Ellison Jr. for a 7-yarder in the fourth, and then ran in the clincher himself from a yard out with 3:49 left. Sean Wilson and Donovan Lewis each caught eight balls. Nick just kept finding them.

But this was a defensive day, too. FIU threw for 313 yards, and we still kept them out of the end zone when it counted most. Jawarren Corbin picked off a throw on their very first drive. Right before halftime, Kevin Moore intercepted one at our goal and brought it out 46 yards. Dominick Brogna broke up a fourth-down throw at our 1 in the second quarter. Gavin Moul was everywhere with 13 tackles, and Blake Matthews kept the quarterback running for his life.

When FIU scored with 5:42 left to make it 17-16, we blocked the extra point. Then Minicucci went right back down the field for the touchdown, and on FIU's last drive the defense got the stop on fourth down with 1:51 to go. We picked up a first down, and that was that.
Tucker Smack hit a 22-yard field goal in the third. Every point mattered today.
One more win and this team is bowl eligible. Newark, can you feel it?

articles.title: Texas A&M vs Tennessee: Aggies Lead at the Half, Then the Offense Disappears
articles.byline: Colt Wendeborn, The Texas A&M Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Tennessee Volunteers (8-2) 22, Texas A&M Aggies (4-6) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Kyle Field, College Station. Next: at Oklahoma, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Memorial Stadium (Norman, OK), Norman
articles.text:
Ags, I stood the whole game like I always do, and by the fourth quarter my knees were telling me what my heart already knew. Tennessee 22, Texas A&M 7. That was Saturday at Kyle Field. It leaves us at 4-6. In front of 108,504 of the most loyal fans in college football, we came up short.

We actually led at halftime. KJ Edwards broke a 25-yard touchdown run early in the second quarter, and it was 7-6 at the break. Our defense was playing tough, hard-nosed football. Dalton Brooks and Tawfiq Byard each made 11 tackles, and Ray Coney had a tackle and a half for loss. Tennessee kept settling for field goals.

But our offense had nothing to give that defense a break. Eight first downs. 179 yards. Marcel Reed went 9 of 22 for 71 yards, and we converted 2 of 11 third downs. Tennessee held the ball for 42 minutes, and that's a lot to ask of any defense. Mario Craver caught five balls for 49 yards, and Rueben Owens II ran hard for 39, but it wasn't enough.

The play that turned the game came early in the fourth quarter. We'd forced a punt, and then a roughing-the-passer flag kept Tennessee's drive alive. They scored a touchdown a few plays later to go up 16-7. Then we went for it on fourth down from our own 34 and came up short, and an interception after that set up another field goal. It snowballed from there.

I don't want to pile on these kids. They played hard. Kyle Field was loud. But 4-6 is not where any Aggie expected to be in mid-November.

We still have time to finish strong, and you know the Twelfth Man will be there.

Gig 'em, Ags. The Texas A&M Aggies travel to face Oklahoma in Norman, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Tennessee vs Texas A&M: Cooper Ranvier Kicks Five and the Vols Grind Out Kyle Field
articles.byline: Earl 'Rocky Top' Haskew, The Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Tennessee Volunteers (8-2) 22, Texas A&M Aggies (4-6) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Kyle Field, College Station. Next: vs LSU, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Neyland Stadium, Knoxville
articles.text:
Vol Nation, it's Rocky Top time in College Station. Tennessee 22, Texas A&M 7 on Saturday at Kyle Field, and we're 8-2 with five wins in our last six. There were 108,504 people in that building, and in the fourth quarter the only ones making noise were wearing orange.

Cooper Ranvier, take a bow. Five field goals, a career high: 23, 30, 32, 44 and 27 yards. Five for five plus an extra point, 16 points from one right foot. When the offense stalled, Cooper cashed it in, and in a game like this, that's the difference.

It was ugly early. We trailed 7-6 at halftime, and nobody did much of anything in the third quarter. Then Ranvier put us ahead 9-7 late in the third. On the next drive, the Aggies were flagged for roughing the passer on what should've been a punt, and we made them pay. Faizon Brandon flipped a 5-yard touchdown to DaSaahn Brame with 9:38 left. 16-7, and the orange section stood up for good.

This was a grind-it-out, own-the-clock kind of day. We held the ball for 42 minutes. DeSean Bishop carried it 34 times for 97 yards, and Javin Gordon added 78 on 11. George MacIntyre was steady, 13 of 17 for 109 yards. Mike Matthews had a 25-yard grab.

The defense? Lights out. Texas A&M had eight first downs and 179 yards. The Aggies converted 2 of 11 third downs and came up short on fourth down in their own end. TJ Metcalf led us with eight tackles and picked off a throw, bringing it back 37 yards to set up a field goal. Dejuan Lane grabbed another with 2:21 left. Arion Carter made seven stops.

Josh Heupel's group isn't always flashy. On Saturday, it was something better: tough.

Checkerboard end zones, a big crowd and a big game. Go Vols! The Tennessee Volunteers host LSU at Neyland Stadium, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: New Mexico State vs Missouri State: 253 Rushing Yards and a Heartbreak in Overtime
articles.byline: Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, The New Mexico State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri State Bears (4-6) 27, New Mexico State Aggies (3-7) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield. Next: vs Delaware, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:00 PM ET, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces
articles.text:
Aggies, I've had a lot of hard nights following this team, and this one goes near the top of the list. Missouri State 27, New Mexico State 21. It took overtime at Robert W. Plaster Stadium, and we're 3-7. We had it. We had it right there.

The ground game was beautiful. James Jones ran 25 times for 150 yards and a 1-yard touchdown early in the fourth that gave us a 21-14 lead. TJ Washington Jr. added 107 yards on 15 carries and caught a 14-yard touchdown from Trey Hedden in the third quarter to tie it. We ran for 253 yards and held the ball for more than 33 minutes. That's Aggie football, the way I like it, green chile tough.

Hedden also found Brodie Malone-Bradford for a 17-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The defense stood up when it counted, too: Tory Gethers had two and a half tackles for loss, De'Marcus Peters picked off a throw in the third quarter and made a fourth-down stop, and we stuffed them on fourth down again in the fourth. Nick Session made six tackles.

But the mistakes. Oh, the mistakes. Missouri State's first touchdown was an interception return. A fumble in the third quarter killed a drive at their 40. Twelve penalties for 115 yards. And with 2:51 left, up seven, we missed a 22-yard field goal that would have just about sealed it. They went 80 yards and tied it with 56 seconds left.

Then in overtime, a throw got picked off and returned 88 yards. It was finished before I could even stand up.

I'm proud of the way this team ran the football. I'm heartbroken about the rest. Las Cruces, we'll be back.

Home cooking. Let's go, Aggies. Pistols up! The New Mexico State Aggies host Delaware at Aggie Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 3 PM ET.

articles.title: Missouri State vs New Mexico State: Joel Boamah's 88-Yard Return Ends It in Overtime
articles.byline: Clementine Bilyeu, The Missouri State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri State Bears (4-6) 27, New Mexico State Aggies (3-7) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield. Next: at Jacksonville State, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville
articles.text:
Bears fans, I have no voice left and I don't care. Missouri State 27, New Mexico State 21 in overtime on Saturday night at Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield, and we're 4-6 and 4-1 at home. The game ended with Joel Boamah sprinting 88 yards with an interception while the whole stadium chased him to the end zone.

Let me back up, because this one was a ride. New Mexico State ran the ball right at us all night, 253 rushing yards, and took a 21-14 lead on a 1-yard run early in the fourth quarter. We came up short on fourth down twice. Then, with 2:51 left, the Aggies lined up for a 22-yard field goal to go up 10, and it missed. I grabbed the stranger next to me by both shoulders.

Henry Belin IV took us 80 yards in eight plays, and Connor Lair ran it in from 5 yards with 56 seconds left. 21-21. Isaiah Myers had five catches for 89 yards, and Mekhi Miller added six. Overtime in Springfield!

Then on the fifth play of overtime, Boamah jumped the throw and took it the length of the field. That kid was everywhere. In the third quarter he forced a fumble and recovered it himself to stop a drive at our 40. Earlier, Dylan Brooks had started our scoring with a 15-yard interception return in the second quarter. Two defensive touchdowns in one game. Jared Lloyd made 15 tackles, and Tim Brantley Jr. had three tackles for loss and a sack. Christian Ford broke up two throws.

Belin went 20 of 37 for 187 yards and threw a 9-yard touchdown to Jmariyae Robinson right before halftime. He took some hits and kept standing in there.

Was it pretty? Nope. But I've been coming to games on this side of town a long time, and I'll remember this one forever.

Bring that same fight on the road, Bears. Go Bears! The Missouri State Bears travel to face Jacksonville State in Jacksonville, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: Sam Houston vs Kennesaw State: A Tough Afternoon in Huntsville, 26-7
articles.byline: Lem Coxwell, The Sam Houston Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kennesaw State Owls (4-6) 26, Sam Houston Bearkats (1-9) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville. Next: vs Middle Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville
articles.text:
Bearkat faithful, it was a long one at Bowers today. Kennesaw State 26, Sam Houston 7. That was Saturday. It leaves us at 1-9. I sat in my usual seat, tipped my cap to Big Sam out on the interstate on the way in, and hoped for better. Didn't get it.

We had a moment early. After Kennesaw went up 10-0, Landyn Locke led a drive and hit Chris Reed for a 10-yard touchdown early in the second quarter. 10-7, and the home crowd got loud. Reed was our best weapon all afternoon with five catches for 48 yards.

Then Kennesaw answered right away with a 6-yard touchdown run, and our offense never found the end zone again. We had 184 yards for the game. Locke went 9 of 15 for 71, and DJ Bailey went 3 of 9. Alton McCaskill ran hard for 53 yards on 10 carries, including a 22-yarder.

The play that broke it came late in the third. We were down 20-7, and we had fourth-and-3 in the red zone. The throw went across the middle, got picked off at their 12 and came back 88 yards for a touchdown. That's a 14-point swing on one snap, and you could feel the air go out of the stadium. Earlier in the quarter, we missed a 45-yard field goal. It just wasn't our day.

The defense fought. Josh Alexander-Felton was disruptive all afternoon with a sack and two and a half tackles for loss. Brian Bates Jr. had six tackles and a tackle and a half for loss. Tyler Bailey made six stops and broke up a throw. Kennesaw went 4 of 13 on third down and only managed 271 yards, so those guys earned their keep.

I'll be back next week. That's what Bearkats do.

Eat 'em up, Kats. The Sam Houston Bearkats host Middle Tennessee at Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: Kennesaw State vs Sam Houston: Cam Miller Goes 88 Yards and the Owls Win a Third Straight
articles.byline: Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, The Kennesaw State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kennesaw State Owls (4-6) 26, Sam Houston Bearkats (1-9) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville. Next: vs Florida International, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:00 PM ET, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw
articles.text:
Owls, three in a row! Kennesaw State 26, Sam Houston 7 on Saturday at Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville, Texas, and we're 4-6 with three straight Conference USA wins. We had never beaten the Bearkats. We were 0-3 against them, all close losses. Not anymore.

The play of the day, maybe the season, belongs to Cam Miller. Late in the third quarter, Sam Houston had fourth-and-3 in the red zone, and Miller jumped the throw across the middle at our 12 and ran 88 yards the other way untouched. I screamed so loud the family next to me moved down a row. 26-7, and that settled it.

Boogie Woods III was a workhorse again, 17 carries for 101 yards, and he caught a 19-yard touchdown from Landon Varnes in the first quarter to make it 10-0. Woods came in leading the conference in rushing touchdowns, and now he's beating teams through the air, too. Brayden Munroe got one carry all day and turned it into a 6-yard touchdown. Talk about efficient.

Varnes was cool and careful, 22 of 35 for 181 yards with no turnovers. Davis Bryson caught six balls for 56 yards. Daniel Kinney hit field goals from 47 and 33 yards.

And the defense? Sam Houston had 184 yards, and after its touchdown early in the second quarter it never scored again. Marcus Patterson got a sack. Josh Anglin made six tackles. Tywon Christopher and Baron Hopson each had a tackle for loss. The Bearkats missed a 45-yard field goal in the third, and then came Miller's interception. Defense wins, y'all.

Remember when we beat Middle Tennessee 44-28 on the road and Delaware 42-40 at home? This streak is real, and the Owls are playing their best football right now.

Let's make it four. Hooty hoo! The Kennesaw State Owls host Florida International at Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Nov. 21, 3 PM ET.

articles.title: Kansas State vs TCU: Grounded Flight, Slow Start, 20-10 Loss in Fort Worth
articles.byline: Hattie Brandvold, The Kansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: TCU Horned Frogs (5-5) 20, Kansas State Wildcats (4-6) 10, Sat., Nov. 14, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth. Next: vs Arizona, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan
articles.text:
Wildcats, what a weekend. Our team couldn't fly out Friday because of the nationwide ground stop, the plane landed in Texas about three hours before kickoff, and then we lost to TCU 20-10 on Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium. We're 4-6. I drove down from Manhattan, so at least my trip went fine.

The first half looked like a team that had just stepped off a plane, because it had. TCU scored on a 19-yard run in the first seven minutes, kicked a field goal, and we were down 10-0 at halftime without much to show. Our first possession of the game ended with a fumble at our own 28. Then TCU scored again on the first drive of the third quarter, and it was 17-0.

That's when the Wildcats finally woke up. Luis Rodriguez boomed a 55-yard field goal, and I let out a holler you could hear in the Flint Hills. Then, late in the third, Dillon Duff dropped a beauty to Jaron Tibbs for a 53-yard touchdown. 17-10, and we were right back in it.

Tibbs was terrific, eight catches for 115 yards. Duff went 22 of 33 for 244 yards with no interceptions. Garrett Oakley caught six. On defense, Asa Newsom made 11 tackles and Wesley Fair had nine.

We just couldn't run it. Fifty-eight rushing yards, with Joe Jackson and Rodney Fields Jr. each getting 33. And TCU converted 10 of 18 third downs, which kept our offense on the sideline far too long. A 36-yard field goal with 10:15 left gave them breathing room, and we fumbled in the final two minutes.

I'm not going to blame the flight for everything. But I'm not going to pretend it didn't matter, either. These kids fought back from 17 down with almost no sleep.

Back home to Manhattan. Every Man A Wildcat. The Kansas State Wildcats host Arizona at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: TCU vs Kansas State: Frogs Win Ugly, and Fort Worth Will Take It
articles.matchup: Final: TCU Horned Frogs (5-5) 20, Kansas State Wildcats (4-6) 10, Sat., Nov. 14, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth. Next: vs Utah, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth
articles.text:
Frog fans, Sonny Dykes said it himself: sometimes you have to win ugly. TCU 20, Kansas State 10 on Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium, and we're 5-5. One more and we're bowl bound. Riff Ram, Bah Bah!

It started like we were going to run them right out of Cowtown. Kari Ashley broke a 19-yard touchdown run less than seven minutes in, and Kyle Lemmermann kicked a 29-yarder to open the second quarter. Then on the first drive after halftime, Jaden Craig found Jacobe Hayes for a 5-yard touchdown, and it was 17-0.

Craig was steady all day, 20 of 34 for 225 yards with no interceptions. Jordan Dwyer caught five balls for 85 yards, including a 41-yarder, and Ed Small added 65 more. And here's the stat I loved the most: we converted 10 of 18 third downs. That's how you keep the chains moving and the other offense on the bench.

Our defense played with an attitude. Kansas State ran for 58 yards, and Dykes said afterward it had been a while since our run defense was that good. Koron Hayward had two and a half tackles for loss and a sack, plus he forced a fumble in the first quarter that P. Cole Jr recovered at their 28. Hudson Hooper got a sack too. Jamel Johnson had a tackle and a half for loss.

Things got a little tight late in the third when K-State hit a 55-yard field goal and a 53-yard touchdown throw to make it 17-10. My Stetson was getting sweaty. Lemmermann settled it with a 36-yarder with 10:15 left, and the defense forced a fumble in the final two minutes to end it.

Credit to the Wildcats, by the way. Their flight got grounded Friday and they landed about three hours before kickoff. That's rough. But a win is a win, and this team needed one.

Big one, Frogs. Fill the place. The TCU Horned Frogs host Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Charlotte vs East Carolina: Aiden Bui Kicks Three, Niners Fall 17-16
articles.matchup: Final: East Carolina Pirates (6-4) 17, Charlotte 49ers (1-9) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte. Next: at Tulsa, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa
articles.text:
Niner Nation, one point. One single point. East Carolina 17, Charlotte 16 on Saturday at Jerry Richardson Stadium, and we're 1-9. I've had a lot of tough Saturdays this fall, but this one is going to sit with me on the drive down Highway 29.

The first half was the best football we've played in weeks. Aiden Bui opened the scoring with a 50-yard field goal. Conner Harrell hit Jaden Barnes for an 11-yard touchdown in the second quarter. Then Bui hit from 27 with 1:09 left and from 37 on the final play of the half. Three for three, and we led 16-7. The student section was bouncing.

And the defense was taking the ball away. Jonathan Patterson picked off a throw in the first quarter and broke up a fourth-down try. Dy'Lon Womack intercepted one at our 11, then recovered a fumble at our 24 right before the half after Gavin Willis knocked it loose. Willis was a beast all afternoon with 13 tackles and two and a half for loss. Kadin Schmitz made 11 tackles, and Collin Gill had a sack.

Derrick Eley gave us some fireworks with four catches for 96 yards, including a 33-yarder. Harrell threw for 161.

But the second half just died on us. We had 22 yards of offense after halftime, and minus-17 on the ground. ECU scored on a direct-snap plunge in the third, kicked a 43-yarder in the fourth, and we never found a first down when it mattered.

Then came the cruelest moment. ECU missed a 31-yarder with 2:12 left, and we got the ball at our 20 with a chance to win. On the very next snap, a tipped throw was picked off. I just sat down and stared at the field.

I'm still coming back. The defense deserves a crowd, and Bui deserves every bit of applause we've got.

Keep swinging, Niners. The Charlotte 49ers travel to face Tulsa in Tulsa, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: East Carolina vs Charlotte: Pirates Hold On 17-16 for a Third Straight Bowl Bid
articles.byline: Bartholomew 'Bart' Quidley, The East Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: East Carolina Pirates (6-4) 17, Charlotte 49ers (1-9) 16, Sat., Nov. 14, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte. Next: at Army, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Michie Stadium, West Point
articles.text:
Arrr, Pirate Nation, that one took a year off my life and I'd give it gladly. East Carolina 17, Charlotte 16 on Saturday at Jerry Richardson Stadium, and we're 6-4. That's three straight wins and our third straight season of bowl eligibility. Greenville, warm up the purple and gold.

We were not good in the first half, and I won't pretend otherwise. Ashton Gray scored on a 7-yard run on the first play of the second quarter, but Charlotte answered with a touchdown throw and three field goals, the last one on the final play of the half, and we trailed 16-7. Two interceptions and a fumble at the 49ers' 24 had me pacing the aisle.

Then the defense slammed the door. Charlotte had 22 yards of offense in the entire second half, with minus-17 on the ground. Twenty-two yards! Kieran Davis had three tackles for loss. Crews Law made nine tackles. Julien Davis got in on a sack. Charlotte converted 3 of 14 third downs all day, and in the second half it couldn't get anything going at all.

Gray did the rest. He took a direct snap and pushed in from a yard out in the third quarter to make it 16-14, and he finished with 88 yards on 24 carries and both of our touchdowns. Early in the fourth, Noah Perez drilled a 43-yard field goal for a 17-16 lead.

Perez missed a 31-yarder with 2:12 left, and my heart sank to my shoes. Then DJ Johnson Jr. picked off a tipped throw on Charlotte's very next snap and ran it back 17 yards to their 12. Jordan Miles had grabbed one of his own in the first quarter. We ran out the clock, and I hugged a man I've never met.

Ugly? Sure. Bowl eligible? Absolutely. I'll take ugly and bowl eligible every time.

Respect to the cadets, and let's make it four straight. Go Pirates! The East Carolina Pirates travel to face Army in West Point, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Arkansas State vs Coastal Carolina: Five Turnovers Sink the Red Wolves
articles.byline: Ty Doucet-Harmon, The Arkansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (4-6) 28, Arkansas State Red Wolves (4-6) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Brooks Stadium (SC), Conway. Next: at Louisiana Tech, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:00 PM ET, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston
articles.text:
Red Wolves, I drove a long way to Conway to watch us hand a game away. Coastal Carolina 28, Arkansas State 21. That was Saturday at Brooks Stadium. It leaves us at 4-6. Five turnovers. Four lost fumbles and an interception. I'll be counting those in my sleep on the ride home to Jonesboro.

The frustrating part is we had this game. Chauncy Cobb ripped off a 17-yard touchdown run in the first quarter to tie it at 7. Timothy Carter punched one in from 3 yards in the second quarter, and we led 14-7. The defense was flying around, and our sideline was loose.

Then the ball started getting away from us. Late in the third quarter, tied 14-14, Trey Owens got sacked and the ball came out, and Coastal went 55 yards the other way for a touchdown. Early in the fourth, an interception. And with 4:00 left, down 28-14, we were at their 3 and fumbled again. That one hurt the most. Points right there for the taking.

Owens battled. He threw for 217 yards, ran for 34, and punched in a 2-yard touchdown with 2:02 left to make it a one-score game. Jaylen Bonelli caught six balls, Hunter Summers four and Jabari Bush had a 27-yarder. We converted 2 of 3 on fourth down and outgained them 325 to 271. You don't lose games like that, unless you give the ball away five times.

Joe Drew was a tackling machine with 14 stops. AG McGhee made 11. Brandon Greil forced a fumble in the second quarter that D. Henderson recovered. Coastal ran for 63 yards against us. The defense was good enough to win.

Hold onto the football, fellas. That's the whole lesson.

Let's go get one, Red Wolves. Howl. The Arkansas State Red Wolves travel to face Louisiana Tech in Ruston, Nov. 21, 7 PM ET.

articles.title: Coastal Carolina vs Arkansas State: Reggie Jean's Scoop and Score Lifts the Chants
articles.byline: Marigold 'Goldie' Seabrook, The Coastal Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (4-6) 28, Arkansas State Red Wolves (4-6) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Brooks Stadium (SC), Conway. Next: at Louisiana, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:00 PM ET, Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette
articles.text:
Chant Nation, teal is the color of happiness tonight. Coastal Carolina 28, Arkansas State 21 on Saturday at Brooks Stadium in Conway, and we're 4-6. A November breeze off the marsh, a sea of teal and a defense that would not stop taking the football. That's my kind of Saturday.

Five takeaways. Five! Arkansas State put the ball on the ground four times and lost all four, and threw an interception, too. The biggest one came late in the third quarter with the game tied 14-14. Ibrahim Diawara came screaming around the corner, sacked Trey Owens and knocked it loose, and Reggie Jean scooped it up and ran 55 yards to the end zone. I nearly fell out of the bleachers.

Deuce Bailey was nearly flawless. Twenty-one of 24 for 208 yards. He threw a 7-yard touchdown to Karmello English in the first quarter, and after Arkansas State went up 14-7, he punched in a 2-yarder himself late in the second to tie it. That was his first rushing touchdown of the season. Colton Hinton caught six balls for 81 yards, and Robby Washington had a 39-yarder.

Kente Edwards put it away with an 11-yard touchdown run with 6:12 left. 28-14, Chants.

The defense was still not done. Zeke Marshall picked off a throw early in the fourth quarter. With 4:00 left and the Red Wolves at our 3, B. Rose fell on a fumble at the 2 to stop another scoring chance. Se'Von McDowell made nine tackles and Marcellius Pulliam had eight. Arkansas State scored with 2:02 left, but that was as close as it got.

We're still fighting for a bowl, and a win like this keeps the dream alive.

Bring the teal to Cajun country. Go Chants! The Coastal Carolina Chanticleers travel to face Louisiana in Lafayette, Nov. 21, 3 PM ET.

articles.title: Temple vs UAB: Curly Ordonez Makes 15 Tackles, Owls Fall 36-10
articles.matchup: Final: UAB Blazers (6-4) 36, Temple Owls (2-8) 10, Sat., Nov. 14, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia. Next: vs Rice, Thu., Nov. 19, 7:30 PM ET, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia
articles.text:
Owls, I bundled up, grabbed a cheesesteak on the way down Broad Street, and sat in the Linc ready for a good one. For a half, we had one. UAB 36, Temple 10 on Saturday at Lincoln Financial Field, and we're 2-8.

It started great. Ajani Sheppard hit JoJo Bermudez for a 12-yard touchdown in the first quarter, and we were up 7-0. Adrian Laing picked off a throw and brought it back 10 yards. Carl Hardin drilled a 44-yard field goal to tie it 10-10 in the second quarter. At halftime it was 13-10, and South Philly was feeling it.

And Curly Ordonez? That man should get a statue next to Rocky. Fifteen tackles, 12 of them solo, a sack and two tackles for loss. Eric Stuart made 12 tackles of his own. Laing added eight to go with the interception. Those guys were out there for 37 minutes and never stopped hitting.

But UAB just kept running. They ran 55 times for 366 yards, and their back went for 202. Every time we got a stop, they came right back at us. A 33-yard touchdown run in the third made it 20-10, a safety in the fourth made it 22-10, and a 54-yarder after that ended the drama.

Our offense couldn't get rolling against that secondary. Sheppard went 11 of 30 for 85 yards, and we converted 2 of 12 third downs. Keveun Mason ran hard for 65 yards on eight carries. We came up empty on fourth down twice late.

I'm not going to pretend 2-8 doesn't hurt. It does. But I'll keep coming down Broad Street every Saturday, because this is my team, and the guys who play their hearts out for 15 tackles deserve a crowd.

A Thursday night at the Linc. Let's show up, Philly. T for Temple U! The Temple Owls host Rice at Lincoln Financial Field, Thursday, Nov. 19, 7:30 PM ET.

But UAB just kept running. They ran 55 times for 366 yards, and their back went for 202. Every time we got a stop, they came right back at us. A 33-yard touchdown run in the third made it 20-10, a safety in the fourth made it 22-10, and a 54-yarder after that ended the drama.

Our offense couldn't get rolling against that secondary. Sheppard went 11 of 30 for 85 yards, and we converted 2 of 12 third downs. Keveun Mason ran hard for 65 yards on eight carries. We came up empty on fourth down twice late.

I'm not going to pretend 2-8 doesn't hurt. It does. But I'll keep coming down Broad Street every Saturday, because this is my team, and the guys who play their hearts out for 15 tackles deserve a crowd.

articles.title: UAB vs Temple: Rod Robinson II Runs for 202 and the Blazers Are Bowl Bound
articles.matchup: Final: UAB Blazers (6-4) 36, Temple Owls (2-8) 10, Sat., Nov. 14, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia. Next: vs UTSA, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Protective Stadium, Birmingham
articles.text:
Blazer Nation, pack a bag. UAB 36, Temple 10 on Saturday at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, and we're 6-4 and bowl eligible for the first time since 2022. I called my brother in Birmingham from the parking lot and we both hollered so loud a cab driver honked at us.

This was Rod Robinson II's day, start to finish. Twenty-two carries, 202 yards, three touchdowns, all career highs. He scored from 9 yards in the first quarter to tie it at 7, from 33 in the third to make it 20-10, and then he broke a 54-yarder in the fourth that had our little corner of the Linc jumping. The junior had never gone for that many yards in an entire season before. Now he did it in one afternoon.

We ran for 366 yards as a team. Bam McReynolds added 60, Ja'Vin Simpkins had 54, and Nate Rogers punched in a 5-yarder late. When you can run like that, you hold the ball for 37 minutes and the other team just sits and watches.

And our defense, the best in the country against the throw, did exactly what it does. Temple completed 11 of 30 throws for 85 yards and converted 2 of 12 third downs. Marlin Dean was a monster: a sack for a safety in the fourth quarter, a fumble recovery in the second, eight tackles and two tackles for loss. D. Gulley forced that fumble. The Owls didn't score after the second quarter.

Jonah Delange hit field goals from 50 and 30 yards. Scott Isacks had a 67-yard catch. Ryder Burton went 11 of 19 for 133 and kept it steady.

Bowl eligible. I keep saying it out loud because I like the way it sounds.

Fill it up, Birmingham. Go Blazers! The UAB Blazers host UTSA at Protective Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.
