articles.title: Vanderbilt vs Alabama: Brock Taylor's Big Leg and a Defense That Fought, in a 21-6 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Alabama Crimson Tide (8-2) 21, Vanderbilt Commodores (4-6) 6, Sat., Nov. 14, FirstBank Stadium, Nashville. Next: at Florida, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville
articles.text:
Commodores, I'm proud of you, even if the scoreboard isn't. Alabama 21, Vanderbilt 6 on Saturday at FirstBank Stadium, and we're 4-6. We held the No. 7 team in the country to 21 points in our house, and I'll be telling everyone on West End about it this week.

Brock Taylor has a cannon attached to his hip. He drilled a 52-yard field goal late in the second quarter for a 3-0 lead, and then a 57-yarder in the third. Fifty-seven! I watched it from the student section and it still had room to spare. Somebody find that young man a bigger stadium to kick in.

Bryan Longwell was the best player on the field for us. Thirteen tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss. Mason Lewis sacked Keelon Russell on a fourth down in the second quarter, and Dontae Carter picked off a throw at the Alabama 20 a few minutes later. In the fourth quarter, T. Carter scooped up a fumble and ran it 21 yards. CJ Heard and Nick Rinaldi made nine tackles each. That defense gave us chance after chance.

The offense just couldn't cash them in. Jared Curtis threw for 223 yards, going 25 of 40, and Junior Sherrill was terrific with seven catches for 100 yards, including a 44-yarder. But we ran for 12 yards on 23 carries, converted 2 of 15 third downs, and came up empty on fourth down three times in the second half. You can't beat Alabama doing that.

The heartbreaker was the sequence right before halftime. We were up 3-0, and Alabama scored with six seconds left. Then it scored again early in the third quarter. That stretch was the game.

Fourteen penalties didn't help, either. That's on us. But this team keeps fighting, and Clark Lea's group still has chances to make some noise.

Anchor Down, Commodores. The Vanderbilt Commodores travel to face Florida in Gainesville, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Alabama vs Vanderbilt: Keelon Russell Shakes Off the Ankle, Tide Grind Out 21-6
articles.matchup: Final: Alabama Crimson Tide (8-2) 21, Vanderbilt Commodores (4-6) 6, Sat., Nov. 14, FirstBank Stadium, Nashville. Next: vs Chattanooga, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:00 PM ET, Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa
articles.text:
Roll Tide, y'all. It wasn't pretty, but neither is my mama's fruitcake, and we eat that every Christmas. Alabama 21, Vanderbilt 6 on Saturday at FirstBank Stadium in Nashville, and we're 8-2.

All week long, we heard Keelon Russell might not go on that ankle. Coach DeBoer said even the last 24 hours were up in the air. Then the young man trotted out there and threw for 217 yards and three touchdowns, 22 of 33, while getting sacked three times. Lotzeir Brooks said it best: Keelon is a dog. In Tuscaloosa, that's a compliment.

The first half was a slog. Vanderbilt kicked a 52-yard field goal, and I was gripping my houndstooth hat with both hands. Then, with six seconds left before halftime, Russell found Marshall Pritchett for a 9-yard touchdown, and we went to the locker room up 7-3. Big, big swing.

Brooks owned the third quarter. He scored twice: a 39-yard catch early in the half and a 9-yarder at 7:13 that made it 21-6. Five catches, 62 yards, two scores. Ryan Coleman-Williams caught seven for 68, and Daniel Hill ran for 89 yards on 14 carries.

Now the defense, which is the reason I'm smiling tonight. Vanderbilt ran for 12 yards. Twelve! The Commodores converted 2 of 15 third downs and came up short on fourth down three times in the second half. QB Reese had a sack and eight tackles, and Dijon Lee Jr. and Red Morgan made seven tackles each. We had five sacks and held Vandy to a season-low 235 yards. That's Alabama defense.

Coach DeBoer wants us finishing teams off better, and he's right. Two turnovers in the second half let Vanderbilt hang around. But a road win in the SEC in November is a road win, and I'll take all of them.

Then comes the one we all circle. Roll Tide Roll. The Alabama Crimson Tide host Chattanooga at Bryant-Denny Stadium, Nov. 21, 2 PM ET.

articles.title: Clemson vs Georgia Tech: Six Points and a Long Walk Down the Hill
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (3-7) 20, Clemson Tigers (6-4) 6, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Clemson, SC), Clemson. Next: at Duke, Fri., Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham
articles.text:
Tiger fans, I rubbed Howard's Rock with both hands today and it didn't help. Georgia Tech 20, Clemson 6. That was Saturday at Memorial Stadium. It leaves us at 6-4. Georgia Tech hadn't won in Death Valley since 2008. I've got grandchildren who weren't born the last time that happened, and now they've seen it.

We just couldn't stop the run. The Yellow Jackets ran 52 times for 269 yards. A 53-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter made it 20-3, and I heard the groans clear up in the upper deck. That's the fourth time this season somebody has run for 190 or more on us, and that is not Clemson football.

The offense never got going. Christopher Vizzina went 12 of 27 for 133 yards with an interception, and Trent Pearman came in for a few series. We ran for 86 yards as a team. Juju Preston had four catches for 56 yards, including a 33-yarder, and Bryant Wesco Jr. caught three. Nolan Hauser was our whole scoring offense with field goals from 40 and 47 yards.

A few guys fought like Tigers. Sammy Brown made 11 tackles and recovered a fumble at our 16 in the fourth quarter to keep it a two-score game. Corey Myrick picked off a throw in the second quarter and broke up two more. Will Heldt had eight tackles. The defense gave us chances. We came up short on fourth down twice and lost the ball on an interception with 4:55 left.

I don't like losing at home. I really don't like losing at home to a team that came in 2-7. But I've been coming to these games for a long, long time, and I'm not going anywhere.

Short week, Tigers. Let's get the taste of this one out of our mouths. Go Tigers. The Clemson Tigers travel to face Duke in Durham, Friday, Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Georgia Tech vs Clemson: The Jackets Run Through Death Valley for the First Time Since 2008
articles.byline: Wendell Quist, The Georgia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (3-7) 20, Clemson Tigers (6-4) 6, Sat., Nov. 14, Memorial Stadium (Clemson, SC), Clemson. Next: vs Wake Forest, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Jackets, I drove up I-85 expecting heartbreak and came home with the best Saturday of the season. Georgia Tech 20, Clemson 6 on Saturday at Memorial Stadium, and that's our first win in Death Valley since 2008. Eighteen years! I was still paying off my slide rule the last time this happened.

Nobody saw this coming, and I don't blame them. We came in 2-7 with four straight losses, all by double digits. Alberto Mendoza said the team knew it was good enough. They burned the boats, he said. Well, they rowed right through Clemson anyway.

We ran for 269 yards. Justice Haynes broke a 53-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter that made it 20-3, and he finished with 116 yards on just 13 carries. Grady Adamson carried it 19 times for 87 yards and opened the scoring with a 3-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Trelain Maddox chipped in 50 more. Old-school, downhill, ram-it-down-their-throats football, the kind that makes engineers weep with joy.

Mendoza threw just 14 times, but he made them count: 138 yards, including a 50-yarder to Chris Corbo and a 37-yarder to Jordan Allen. Aidan Birr hit field goals from 24 and 22 yards.

And the defense! Clemson managed 228 yards and 86 on the ground. Cayman Spaulding was a monster with 11 tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss, and he knocked the ball loose on a fourth-down stop in the first quarter. Taje McCoy got a sack. Kealan Jones picked off a throw with 4:55 left at midfield, and Tawfiq Thomas stuffed the final fourth-down try. Clemson's only points came on two field goals. Two!

It's been a hard year on the Flats. Today was a reminder of why we love this team anyway.

Bring that same energy home, Jackets. The Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets host Wake Forest at Bobby Dodd Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Rutgers vs Nebraska: A Long, Scoreless Afternoon in Piscataway
articles.matchup: Final: Nebraska Cornhuskers (6-4) 31, Rutgers Scarlet Knights (2-8) 0, Sat., Nov. 14, SHI Stadium, Piscataway. Next: at Penn State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Beaver Stadium, University Park
articles.text:
Knights, I'm going to be straight with you, the way my old man was straight with me at the diner after every bad Saturday. Nebraska 31, Rutgers 0, in Piscataway. We're 2-8. Zero points at home. There's no Jersey way to spin that, and I won't try.

Coach Schiano said it after the game: when it rains, it pours. It poured. We had 143 yards. We converted 1 of 11 third downs. AJ Surace went 4 of 12 for 24 yards with two interceptions, and Sean Ashenfelder came in and went 3 of 4. Nebraska got two long drives of 94 and 90 yards, and we didn't have an answer for either one.

There were a few guys who played their hearts out, and I want to name them. JJ Conyers made nine tackles and broke up a throw. Devonte Anderson and Sean Allison had eight tackles each, with a tackle for loss apiece. Allison stuffed a fourth-down run in the third quarter. Moses Walker added six tackles. Clay Thevenin ran hard for 43 yards on 10 carries, and Antwan Raymond kept fighting for every inch.

We stopped Nebraska on fourth down twice in the third quarter. The defense kept it at 14-0 at the half and 21-0 after three. If the offense could have found one spark, one big play, the Banks might have woken up. It never came.

Earlier this week the school announced Schiano is coming back next season, and he said he believes in the young players and the guys returning. I believe in them, too. This program has been down before, and Schiano is the man who picked it up the first time.

For today, though, I'm going to drive up Route 18, grab a fat sandwich, and try to forget the scoreboard.

Chop on, Knights. Better days are coming. The Rutgers Scarlet Knights travel to face Penn State in University Park, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Nebraska vs Rutgers: A 31-0 Shutout Snaps the Skid in Piscataway
articles.matchup: Final: Nebraska Cornhuskers (6-4) 31, Rutgers Scarlet Knights (2-8) 0, Sat., Nov. 14, SHI Stadium, Piscataway. Next: vs Ohio State, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE), Lincoln
articles.text:
Husker Nation, breathe it in. Nebraska 31, Rutgers 0 on Saturday at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, and the four-game skid is history. We're 6-4, and the Blackshirts just threw our first conference shutout since 2003. The last time we pitched one on the road in league play was 1997. I was a kid in pigtails at a watch party in Kearney.

Let's start with the defense, because it earned the top billing. Rutgers had 143 yards. Forty-two through the air. The Scarlet Knights converted 1 of 11 third downs, and when they did get close, we slammed the door. Caleb Benning picked off a throw at our 10 in the third quarter and brought it back 39 yards. Jeremiah Charles grabbed another at our 18 in the fourth. Vincent Shavers Jr. had 10 tackles, and Cameron Lenhardt made two tackles for loss.

Anthony Colandrea was in complete command. Fifteen of 22 for 188 yards, two touchdown throws and a 6-yard touchdown run, plus 66 yards on the ground. He hit Luke Lindenmeyer for a 15-yarder with 20 seconds left in the first quarter, and Carter Nelson for a 13-yarder early in the fourth.

articles.title: Miami vs Duke: Mensah Beats His Old School, Canes Move a Step Closer to Charlotte
articles.byline: Javi 'The Breeze' Castillo, The Miami Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Miami Hurricanes (9-1) 36, Duke Blue Devils (7-3) 25, Sat., Nov. 14, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens. Next: vs Virginia Tech, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Canes, the breeze off the Glades felt extra good this afternoon. Miami 36, Duke 25. That was Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium. It leaves us at 9-1, 7-0 in the ACC, with 11 straight conference wins. That ties a school record. Charlotte, warm up the stadium. We're coming.

This one had a little extra seasoning. Darian Mensah led Duke to the ACC title last year, and on Saturday he lined up against the Blue Devils in orange and green and carved them up. Thirty of 41 for 382 yards. He said afterward it felt a little weird. Brother, it felt amazing from where I sat.

And Cooper Barkate, another former Blue Devil, had his first 100-yard game in a Miami uniform: eight catches for 134 yards. That's what we call a homecoming in reverse.

Javian Mallory was the hero of the second half. He caught a 63-yard touchdown from Mensah late in the third quarter to make it 22-10, then ran one in from 2 yards and broke a 39-yarder with 4:21 left that iced it. Three touchdowns, 150 yards from scrimmage, and a whole section of Hard Rock chanting his name. Mark Fletcher Jr. punched in a 4-yarder in the second quarter, too.

Jake Weinberg deserves a parade. Three field goals, from 39, 26 and 24 yards, and three extra points. When the offense stalled early, he kept us ahead.

I'll be honest: Nate Sheppard gave our defense fits. Two 47-yard runs, 12 catches, the whole show. That kid is special. But Mohamed Toure made 11 tackles, 10 of them solo, and Xavier Lucas picked off Walker Eget with 6:57 left to snuff out Duke's last real push. We held the ball for more than 34 minutes and gained 532 yards.

Manny Diaz came back to Hard Rock with a good team, and I respect it. But this is our house, and we're 5-0 in it.

It's all in front of us, Canes. Let's keep rolling. The Miami Hurricanes host Virginia Tech at Hard Rock Stadium, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Duke vs Miami: Nate Sheppard Puts On a Show, Blue Devils Fall 36-25
articles.byline: Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, The Duke Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Miami Hurricanes (9-1) 36, Duke Blue Devils (7-3) 25, Sat., Nov. 14, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens. Next: vs Clemson, Fri., Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham
articles.text:
Fellow Dukies, I'll keep my composure, as a Wexley-Moore must. Miami 36, Duke 25 on Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium, and we're 7-3. It's an awkward thing to watch your old quarterback throw for 382 yards against you. It's more awkward when your old receiver catches 134 of them. Grandfather would have had words.

Now, let me tell you about Nate Sheppard, because the country needs to know. Sixteen carries for 131 yards and two touchdowns. Twelve catches for 93 yards. He threw a couple of times for 16 more. That's 240 yards of offense from one young man against the best defense in the conference, the first player to run for that many on Miami since September 2024. Manny Diaz called him one of the best players in the United States, and Coach does not hand out compliments like Halloween candy.

Sheppard's 47-yard touchdown run tied it at 10 late in the second quarter, and I may have spilled my iced tea. After Miami pulled away to 22-10, he scored again from 5 yards out with 41 seconds left in the third to make it 22-17. We had a game in Miami Gardens.

Walker Eget threw for 195 yards and found Jeremiah Hasley for a 1-yard touchdown with 21 seconds left, then hit Sheppard for the two-point conversion. Gavin Strange kicked a 37-yard field goal in the second quarter. On defense, Evan Smith made 11 tackles and Andrew Pellicciotta had 10.

The difference was what came after we got close. Miami answered with a 2-yard run, we threw an interception at their 31 with 6:57 left, and then Javian Mallory broke a 39-yard touchdown run. Miami held the ball for more than 34 minutes and piled up 532 yards. That's a lot of time standing on the sideline in the Florida sun.

No shame in losing at Hard Rock to a team that's 9-1. We go home with heads up and our running back's highlight tape.

A Friday night in Durham. Let's make it loud, Blue Devils. The Duke Blue Devils host Clemson at Wallace Wade Stadium, Friday, Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: UConn vs James Madison: Osborne, Bowers and a 100-Yard Return Fuel a 46-22 Win
articles.matchup: Final: UConn Huskies (5-5) 46, James Madison Dukes (8-3) 22, Sat., Nov. 14, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford. Next: vs Old Dominion, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford
articles.text:
Huskies, that's how you do it. UConn 46, James Madison 22. That was Saturday at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in East Hartford. It leaves us at 5-5. JMU came in at 8-2 with a big reputation. It left with a long bus ride back to the Shenandoah Valley.

Kalieb Osborne was close to perfect. Sixteen of 20 for 274 yards and three touchdowns, plus 88 rushing yards on 16 keepers. When JMU went ahead 13-10 late in the second quarter, he needed three snaps to answer, hitting Shamar Porter for a 67-yard touchdown that put us ahead for good. Porter finished with four catches for 135 yards. Four catches! The man doesn't waste them.

Cyncir Bowers was the hammer. Twenty-five carries for 123 yards and three touchdowns: a 9-yard run late in the third, a 2-yard catch in the fourth and a 17-yard run with 2:39 left to finish it. JD Willoughby added a 35-yard touchdown catch, and our offense rolled up 504 yards.

And then there's Ky Wilson. Late in the first quarter, right after JMU took a 6-3 lead, he took the kickoff and went 100 yards the other way. First touchdown of the season for him, and I'm still hearing the roar in my ears. That flipped the whole afternoon.

Hayden Pegg was everywhere on defense with 11 tackles, a sack and an interception right before halftime, and Mike Baker kicked a 21-yarder on the final play of the half to make it 20-13. JMU's JC Evans threw for 236 yards and ran for two scores, so credit where it's due, but we never gave it back to them. Zero turnovers for the Huskies.

This is UConn football in November, and it's fun again.

One more win gets us to six. Let's pack the place, Husky Nation. The UConn Huskies host Old Dominion at Pratt & Whitney Stadium, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: James Madison vs UConn: Dukes Can't Slow Osborne in a 46-22 Loss
articles.byline: Lila Shenandoah, The James Madison Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UConn Huskies (5-5) 46, James Madison Dukes (8-3) 22, Sat., Nov. 14, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford. Next: vs Coastal Carolina, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Bridgeforth Stadium, Harrisonburg
articles.text:
Dukes, I'm not going to dress this up. UConn 46, James Madison 22 on Saturday at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in East Hartford, and we're 8-3. I drove up from Harrisonburg with my purple scarf and a lot of hope, and Connecticut sent me home with a long drive to think.

It started fine. After UConn's opening field goal, JC Evans punched in a 1-yard touchdown run, and we led 6-3. Then, on the very next play, the kickoff went 100 yards the wrong way. That's the kind of thing you can't give a team at home.

We came back, though. Late in the second quarter, Evans hit Braeden Wisloski for a 16-yard touchdown, and we were up 13-10. For about 30 seconds, all was right in the Valley. Then UConn hit a 67-yard touchdown three snaps later, kicked a field goal at the end of the half and never looked back.

Evans battled all day. He threw for 236 yards, ran for two scores and took some hits along the way. Wisloski had seven catches for 75 yards. Cole Keller and Corey Scott made some big grabs, and Morgan Suarez hit a 36-yard field goal in the fourth. On defense, Seth Gathers made 10 tackles and Nakian Jackson had nine with a sack.

But the penalties killed us. Thirteen of them for 130 yards. You can't play like that on the road against a quarterback who completed 16 of 20 throws. UConn put up 504 yards, and we didn't force a single turnover.

This one's going to sting through the open week. But eight wins is eight wins, and this program still has a lot to play for. The Dukes don't stay down long.

Two weeks to get right, Harrisonburg. Go Dukes! The James Madison Dukes host Coastal Carolina at Bridgeforth Stadium, Nov. 28, time TBA.

articles.title: SMU vs Wake Forest: A Rough Ford Stadium Finale for the Mustangs
articles.matchup: Final: Wake Forest Demon Deacons (9-1) 49, SMU Mustangs (7-3) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Gerald J. Ford Stadium, Dallas. Next: at Notre Dame, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame
articles.text:
Mustangs, I wore my best red and blue to the Ford Stadium finale, and I'm going to go hang it in the back of the closet for a while. Wake Forest 49, SMU 7 on Saturday on the Hilltop, and we're 7-3. That's our first ACC loss at home ever, after a 12-0 run in league games on our own field. It had to end sometime. I just wish it hadn't ended like this.

It got away from us fast. Wake scored on a 27-yard run on third-and-18, then added another, and by halftime it was 42-0. Four of their first-half touchdowns came on third down, and we couldn't get off the field. They held the ball for almost 37 minutes. That's a long afternoon for a defense, and ours looked tired by the second quarter.

Kevin Jennings battled. He threw for 209 yards and found Yannick Smith for a 19-yard touchdown late in the third quarter, our only score. Jennings has been one of the great quarterbacks in this program's history, and he's now 16-2 at home in his career. One bad afternoon doesn't change that, and I'll stand up for him all day.

Randy Pittman Jr. caught five balls for 76 yards, and Yamir Knight added five more. Brandon Booker led the defense with eight tackles, and he recovered a fumble after A. Moses knocked it loose in the third quarter. Moses also broke up a fourth-down throw. There were a few fights left in us.

But we gave the ball away three times, ran for 66 yards and converted 3 of 14 third downs. You can't do that against a team that's won seven straight.

I'm still proud of where this program is. Three years in the ACC, a home record most schools would kill for, and a group of seniors who gave Dallas a lot of great Saturdays. Pony Up, always.

Shake this off, Mustangs. A big stage is waiting. The SMU Mustangs travel to face Notre Dame in Notre Dame, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Wake Forest vs SMU: 42-0 at the Half, Seven Straight, and a Message for the Committee
articles.byline: Eloise Brightman-Rowe, The Wake Forest Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Wake Forest Demon Deacons (9-1) 49, SMU Mustangs (7-3) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Gerald J. Ford Stadium, Dallas. Next: at Georgia Tech, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Deacs, are they paying attention now? Wake Forest 49, SMU 7 on Saturday at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas. That's seven straight wins, we're 9-1 and 5-0 on the road, and the Mustangs had never lost an ACC game at home until we showed up. I'd roll the Quad tonight if I weren't stuck in Texas.

It was 42-0 at halftime. Let me say that again for the folks in the back: 42-0, at halftime, against a ranked team, in its building. Ty Clark III started it with a 27-yard touchdown run on third-and-18, and four of our first-half touchdowns came on third down. Jamar Searcy ripped off a 38-yard run on fourth-and-1 that set up another. Carlos Hernandez caught a 44-yard touchdown from Gio Lopez. We were converting everything.

Gio was terrific. He went 14 of 25 for 201 yards and a score and ran for two more touchdowns, both from 5 yards out. We finished 10 of 15 on third down and held the ball for almost 37 minutes. Steele Pizzella came in and added a 25-yard touchdown run in the fourth for good measure.

And the defense? Aiden Hall picked off Kevin Jennings in the first quarter. We stuffed SMU on fourth down at its own 26. D. Afalava and K. Dembele each recovered fumbles. SMU ran for 66 yards and converted 3 of 14 third downs. The Mustangs didn't score until late in the third quarter, and by then the Ford Stadium crowd was heading for the exits.

Jake Dickert said this week that eventually people are going to have to say we're good. Two days after signing his extension, his team made that case about as loudly as a team can. The only loss on our schedule is to Miami, and I would love a second crack at them in Charlotte.

Keep stacking them, Deacs. Go Deacs! The Wake Forest Demon Deacons travel to face Georgia Tech in Atlanta, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Iowa State vs Cincinnati: Aiden Flora Runs Wild Before Ames Finishes Brunch
articles.byline: Twyla Hemmingsen, The Iowa State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa State Cyclones (5-5) 41, Cincinnati Bearcats (5-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames. Next: at UCF, Fri., Nov. 20, 6:00 PM ET, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando
articles.text:
Cyclone Nation, the 11 a.m. kickoff was worth every early alarm. Iowa State 41, Cincinnati 13 on Saturday at Jack Trice Stadium, and we're 5-5 and 5-1 at home. I barely had time to finish my breakfast casserole before Aiden Flora had three touchdowns.

Three touchdowns. In the first quarter. Flora ran it in from 11 yards, then broke a 77-yarder that had the whole east side on its feet, then added a 5-yarder before the first quarter was even done. He also caught a couple, threw one for 37 yards, and by the end of the day he had 216 rushing yards on 28 carries. The former walk-on from right here in our program has now gone for 200 three times this season. Somebody check that young man's legs for springs.

Jaylen Raynor ran the show beautifully. He hit Cameron Pettaway for a 70-yard touchdown on the first play of the second quarter, and it was 28-7 before most of Ames had found its seats. Raynor finished with 229 yards through the air. Jamal Polite Jr. and Vince Benetti each had big grabs, and Arnold Barnes III put a bow on it with a 32-yard touchdown run with 1:40 left.

The defense bent but didn't let Cincinnati back in. The Bearcats ran for 273 yards, and that number made me grumpy, but they went 2 of 10 on third down and 1 of 5 on fourth. Sullivan Schlimgen and Beau Goodwin had nine tackles each, Drew Surges made the stop on fourth down before halftime, and Z. Hawk scooped up a fumble in the fourth quarter. After their touchdown late in the second quarter, Cincinnati didn't score again.

Our offense piled up 551 yards, the fourth time this year we've cleared 500. Kyle Konrardy missed a couple of field goals, but he still hit from 22 and 24 and every extra point, so we'll forgive him and buy him a pork tenderloin.

Jimmy Rogers talked after the game about finding different ways to get Flora the ball. Mission accomplished, Coach.

Pack the sunscreen, Clones. Bowl eligibility is one win away. The Iowa State Cyclones travel to face UCF in Orlando, Friday, Nov. 20, 6 PM ET.

articles.title: Cincinnati vs Iowa State: Cole Tabb Runs for 165, Bearcats Fall 41-13 in Ames
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa State Cyclones (5-5) 41, Cincinnati Bearcats (5-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames. Next: vs Colorado, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati
articles.text:
Bearcats fans, I drove nine hours to Ames with a cooler of Skyline in the trunk, and for about five minutes it was the best decision of my life. Then Aiden Flora happened. Iowa State 41, Cincinnati 13 on Saturday at Jack Trice Stadium, and we're 5-5.

We started like we meant it. JC French IV marched us right down the field and hit Lyviel Waters for a 4-yard touchdown on the opening drive. 7-0, and I was hollering in a sea of cardinal and gold. Then Flora scored three times before the first quarter was done, and a 70-yard throw on the first snap of the second made it 28-7. That's the ballgame in a nutshell, and I hate nutshells.

Cole Tabb was the one bright light, and he was bright. Sixteen carries for 165 yards, including a 66-yard burst, and he caught eight balls for 70 more. Cincinnati ran for 273 yards as a team. Gi'Bran Payne chipped in 46. We could move the ball. We just couldn't finish, going 2 of 10 on third down and 1 of 5 on fourth.

Our lone touchdown after the opening drive was a fun one. Malachi Henry threw a 12-yard touchdown to JC French IV himself late in the second quarter, a little trickery that made me smile through the pain. The extra point missed, so it was 31-13 at the half.

Jasper Beeler was everywhere with 11 tackles and a sack, and Damaine Wilson had 10. Kenny Worthy picked off a throw right before halftime. But Iowa State put up 551 yards, and nobody's winning in Ames giving that up.

The road has been rough, and there's no sugarcoating it: that's six straight road losses. But this team still has a shot at six wins, and Scott Satterfield's group will play hard. It always does.

Back home, Cincinnati. Let's fill it up and send these seniors out right. The Cincinnati Bearcats host Colorado at Nippert Stadium, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Ohio State vs Northwestern: Jeremiah Smith Breaks the Big Ten Record in a 28-19 Win
articles.byline: Brecken 'Buck' Holloway, The Ohio State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio State Buckeyes (7-3) 28, Northwestern Wildcats (6-4) 19, Sat., Nov. 14, Ohio Stadium, Columbus. Next: at Nebraska, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE), Lincoln
articles.text:
Back on track, Buckeye Nation. Ohio State 28, Northwestern 19. The two-game skid is done. We're 7-3, and 101,256 of us got to watch history in the Horseshoe on a November afternoon.

Jeremiah Smith is now the Big Ten's career leader in receiving yards. He moved past Purdue's John Standeford in the second quarter, and I may have shed a single tear into my buckeye necklace. He finished with 11 catches for 117 yards, his 17th 100-yard game, and a touchdown in the fourth quarter that made it 28-13. The foam fingers that said JJ 4 It All were everywhere after the final whistle, and I want one for my mailbox.

Luke Fahey keeps growing up. The freshman threw for 201 yards and three touchdowns: a 4-yarder to Isaiah West, an 8-yarder to Devin McCuin late in the third and the one to Smith. Yes, our first drive ended with an interception near their goal, but he shook it off like a veteran.

Bo Jackson was the hammer. Twenty carries, 114 yards and a 2-yard touchdown before halftime. When it was cold and the Wildcats were hanging around, we just handed it to Bo and let him wear them down one carry at a time.

On defense, Kenyatta Jackson Jr. had two sacks. Qua Russaw had three tackles for loss and broke up the fourth-down throw with 4:06 left that ended Northwestern's last real chance. They ran for 53 yards all day. That's a defense that remembers who it is.

I'm not handing out perfect grades. We lost two fumbles, and Northwestern kept it closer than it should have been, cutting it to 14-13 in the third quarter. But a win is a win in the Horseshoe in November, and Ryan Day's group needed this one.

O-H! The Ohio State Buckeyes travel to face Nebraska in Lincoln, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Northwestern vs Ohio State: Wildcats Hang Tough in the Horseshoe, Fall 28-19
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio State Buckeyes (7-3) 28, Northwestern Wildcats (6-4) 19, Sat., Nov. 14, Ohio Stadium, Columbus. Next: at Minnesota, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
Wildcats, I'm proud and I'm annoyed, and I think that's the right way to feel. Ohio State 28, Northwestern 19 on Saturday at Ohio Stadium, and we're 6-4. We went into a building with 101,256 people and led twice. Twice! Somebody tell Evanston.

Jackson Kleather was money. He kicked a 44-yarder in the first quarter for a 3-0 lead and then a 46-yarder in the second to make it 6-7. On the Buckeyes' first possession of the game, Braden Turner intercepted a throw at our 9 and brought it back to the 28, and the purple in the upper deck got loud.

Coming out of halftime down 14-6, Nicco Marchiol led us on a drive and plowed in from 2 yards out himself to make it 14-13. For a few minutes in the third quarter, I truly believed. Marchiol finished with 225 yards through the air, and he never threw an interception against that defense. Luke Dehnicke caught five for 88 yards and took the last snap of the game into the end zone from 17 yards out, a little reminder that we don't quit.

Robert Fitzgerald made 11 tackles and Jack Sadowsky V had nine. Turner wasn't done, either: he recovered a fumble at our 16 with 1:05 left. He had a day.

The problem was the run game. We had 53 rushing yards. Caleb Komolafe got 54 of them, which tells you how the rest went. Against Ohio State, if you can't run, you're living on third down, and we went 6 of 15. Their fourth-quarter touchdown to Jeremiah Smith made it 28-13, and that was that.

Still, this team went into Columbus and made the Buckeyes sweat into the fourth quarter. Six wins in mid-November. I'll take that and a hot chocolate back in Evanston.

Go 'Cats. The Northwestern Wildcats travel to face Minnesota in Minneapolis, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Maryland vs Wisconsin: Cardell Williams Goes 21 of 23 in His First Start
articles.matchup: Final: Maryland Terrapins (4-6) 24, Wisconsin Badgers (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, SECU Stadium, College Park. Next: at USC, Sat., Nov. 21, 6:15 PM ET, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles
articles.text:
Terps, pinch me. Maryland 24, Wisconsin 21. For the first time since 2023, we've won back-to-back conference games. It took 32 games to get here. I've been waiting so long I nearly forgot what the second one feels like. It feels like crab cakes and fireworks.

And the man who did it was making his first start for us. Cardell Williams, the transfer from Sacramento State, stepped in for an injured Malik Washington and went 21 of 23 for 183 yards. He hit 19 throws in a row at one point, breaking the program record. He also ran in two short touchdowns, a 1-yarder in the second quarter and a 3-yarder in the third. Not bad for a Saturday afternoon debut in College Park.

We were down 21-14 early in the fourth quarter, and I'll admit I got quiet. Then the defense got Wisconsin off the field twice in a row, and Cardell found Preston Howard running free down the right sideline for a 39-yard touchdown with 2:11 left. Tie game. Howard finished with four catches for 77 yards, and that one will be on a highlight loop in my house all week.

Then Trey Reddick came off the blind side and knocked the ball out of the quarterback's hands, and Eyan Thomas fell on it at the Wisconsin 33 with 1:52 left. Five straight Cardell runs later, Sean O'Haire calmly knocked through a 30-yard field goal with 29 seconds on the clock. SECU Stadium exploded.

The defense was the reason we had a chance at all. Wisconsin managed 201 yards and converted 2 of 12 third downs. Daniel Wingate forced and recovered a fumble in the third quarter. Jamare Glasker had three tackles for loss and a sack. Lavon Johnson recovered a fumble in the first quarter, too. Three takeaways, all on the ground.

Interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim said this group believes as long as there are seconds on the clock. I believe it now, too.

Fear the Turtle, coast to coast. The Maryland Terrapins travel to face USC in Los Angeles, Nov. 21, 6:15 PM ET.

articles.title: Wisconsin vs Maryland: Three Fumbles and a Late Field Goal Sink the Badgers
articles.matchup: Final: Maryland Terrapins (4-6) 24, Wisconsin Badgers (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, SECU Stadium, College Park. Next: at Purdue, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette
articles.text:
Badger fans, I'm going to need a long drive home through the cornfields to process this one. Maryland 24, Wisconsin 21 on Saturday at SECU Stadium, and we're 6-4. We had this game in our hands with two minutes left, and we dropped it. Literally, three times.

It started the way I like it. Darrion Dupree ran it in from 4 yards out on our opening possession, and Gavin Lahm kicked a 37-yard field goal in the second quarter. 10-0. Then our defense came up huge right before halftime when Maryland's quarterback fumbled at our 2 and M. Jung pounced on it. That's Wisconsin football, right there.

Mason Posa was a one-man wrecking crew. Thirteen tackles, a sack and two and a half tackles for loss. Cooper Catalano added 10 tackles. Maryland converted 2 of 13 third downs, and if you'd told me that before the game, I'd have started planning a party.

Early in the fourth quarter, Dupree plowed in from a yard out for his second touchdown, and Ryan Hopkins found Eugene Hilton Jr. for the two-point conversion. 21-14, Badgers. Lahm had already hit a 42-yarder in the third. Our freshman quarterback was growing up right in front of us.

Then it unraveled. Maryland hit a 39-yard touchdown down the sideline with 2:11 left. On our next drive, Hopkins got hit from the blind side, the ball came loose, and Maryland recovered at our 33. They ran it five straight times and kicked a 30-yarder with 29 seconds left.

Three fumbles lost. That's the whole story. We held Maryland to 290 yards and still found a way to lose, which is a special kind of painful. Hopkins went 11 of 22 for 77 yards, and the young man will be better for this. He has to be.

Hang onto the football, boys. Grab a brat, Madison. We'll get the next one. The Wisconsin Badgers travel to face Purdue in West Lafayette, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: NC State vs Syracuse: Wolfpack Let a 15-Point Lead Slip in the Home Finale
articles.byline: Rutherford 'Ruff' Pegram, The NC State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Syracuse Orange (5-5) 34, NC State Wolfpack (4-6) 31, Sat., Nov. 14, Carter-Finley Stadium, Raleigh. Next: at Florida State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee
articles.text:
Pack, I don't even know where to start. Syracuse 34, NC State 31 on Saturday at Carter-Finley Stadium, our home finale, and we're 4-6. A day after the school told us Philip Rivers is coming home to coach next season, this was supposed to be a party. For three quarters, it was.

That third quarter was some of the most fun I've had in Raleigh all year. CJ Bailey hit Chance Robinson for a 12-yard score to start it. Davion Gause punched in a 2-yarder. Then Jayden Scott broke loose for a 32-yard touchdown run, and we were up 28-13 heading to the fourth. Scott finished with 127 yards on 14 carries, and every time he touched it, the student section stood up.

Bailey was good, too. He ran for a 9-yard touchdown in the second quarter and finished with 56 rushing yards to go with 211 through the air. Davion Dozier caught one ball all day, and it went for 69 yards. That's how you make a catch count.

King Mack and Jordan Moreta made 10 tackles each, and Brody Barnhardt had nine. Kanoah Vinesett kicked a 21-yard field goal with 6:55 left to make it 31-20, and I thought we were home free.

articles.title: LSU vs Texas: Three Seconds From a Win in Death Valley
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (8-2) 22, LSU Tigers (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Tiger Stadium (LA), Baton Rouge. Next: at Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Neyland Stadium, Knoxville
articles.text:
Tiger fans, I don't know what to say. Texas 22, LSU 21. That was Saturday night at Tiger Stadium. It leaves us at 6-4. We led for most of the night. We led with 3 seconds left. And then we didn't. More than 102,000 of us went silent all at once.

Here's how close it was. Texas got the ball at its own 42, down 21-16, with 2:19 left. They went 58 yards in 12 plays, converted three third downs, and with 3 seconds left, their quarterback found a running back along the sideline for a 4-yard touchdown. They added the two-point try, and that was the ballgame. I sat in my seat for 20 minutes after.

And it hurts because so much went right. Sam Leavitt completed 27 of 37 throws for 244 yards and two touchdowns, both to Jackson Harris, from 10 and 9 yards. Harris caught eight balls. Eugene Wilson III had seven for 96. Dilin Jones ran 19 times for 125 yards, and his 44-yard touchdown run in the third quarter made it 21-10. That run had Death Valley shaking.

Our defense was terrific too. Ty Benefield intercepted two throws, and his first return set up Harris's second touchdown. DJ Pickett intercepted another one at our 8 in the fourth quarter. Davhon Keys made 10 tackles, and Princewill Umanmielen and Ty Benefield each had a sack. Tamarcus Cooley made eight stops.

But we threw three interceptions too, two of them in the Texas end zone. We missed a field goal at the end of the first half. And they kicked three. Those points add up.

Six and four. This one is going to hurt for a long time.

We have to get back up. Geaux Tigers. The LSU Tigers travel to face Tennessee in Knoxville, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: Texas vs LSU: Arch Manning Finds Raleek Brown With 3 Seconds Left in Death Valley
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (8-2) 22, LSU Tigers (6-4) 21, Sat., Nov. 14, Tiger Stadium (LA), Baton Rouge. Next: vs Arkansas, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin
articles.text:
Longhorn Nation, I cannot breathe. Texas 22, LSU 21 on Saturday night at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, and we're 8-2 and unbeaten on the road. More than 102,000 people, the loudest stadium in America, and Arch Manning walked in and won it with 3 seconds left. Hook 'em forever.

Let me take you through the drive, because I'll be telling my grandkids about it. Down 21-16, we got the ball at our 42 with 2:19 left. Manning went to work. Ryan Wingo caught four balls on that drive alone. Manning picked up two first downs with his own legs. Then, from the LSU 4, with 3 seconds on the clock, he found Raleek Brown along the left sideline for the touchdown. Twelve plays, 58 yards. We added the two-point try, and it was 22-21. I tripped on a chair. I don't care.

Manning grew up in Louisiana and went to games in this stadium as a kid. His grandfather and uncle had their own moments here. Now he has his. He also ran in a 1-yard score in the first quarter. He did throw three interceptions, and I won't pretend those didn't scare me. But he made the plays when they mattered.

Gianni Spetic kept us in it with three field goals, from 42, 41 and 50 yards. And Jelani McDonald was a one-man wall on defense. Three interceptions! Two of them came in our end zone. He also made 11 tackles. Rasheem Biles had 11 tackles, a sack and two hurries. Justin Cryer and Bo Mascoe each had a sack too.

Wingo finished with six catches for 68 yards. Jermaine Bishop Jr. had a 32-yard grab. We won with 273 yards of offense because our defense took the ball away three times and our quarterback didn't blink at the end.

Eight and two. Death Valley, conquered.

Back home in Austin. Hook 'em, Horns! The Texas Longhorns host Arkansas at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET.
